We know everyone's on the edge of their seat about the Retention & Severance Plan, so here’s the latest episode in our continuing saga.

As many of you know, we’ve been deep in discussions—sometimes deeper than we’d like—with members of the Creditors' Committee and their consultants since December, cooking up a Retention & Severance Plan. We formally presented the plan to the committee on Friday, February 22. (We brought our best spreadsheets.)

Our dream was that the committee would approve the plan faster than you can say "bankruptcy court," so we could file, finalize, and share all the juicy details with you by the end of the month. We know many of you have career options beyond Enron—hard to believe, but true—and that this plan might just tip the scales on whether you stay for the drama or find a quieter workplace.

Here comes the not-so-fun part: approval of the plan for debtor companies is, sadly, delayed. (Insert collective sigh here.) If there’s one thing we’re learning, it’s that in bankruptcy, things move at glacial speed. If you blink, you definitely won’t miss anything.

The committee did raise some concerns about our proposed plan, but we’re confident we can work it out. After all, we’re getting pretty good at navigating these conversations—practice makes perfect! The Creditors’ Committee is on board in principle, and these plans are pretty standard stuff in the world of bankruptcy. They're designed to both save and maximize what’s left in the company cookie jar.

The Creditors’ Committee also realizes that time is of the essence (we may have reminded them once or twice). They’ve put together a subcommittee to fast-track the review process, and we are meeting with them regularly—yes, we’re as excited for these meetings as you’d expect.

Rest assured, this is priority number one around here—right up there with fixing the coffee machine.

When we filed for bankruptcy, we had no idea just how painfully drawn-out developing a plan could be. Management may have been a tad optimistic—call it a New Year’s resolution gone wrong. What we’ve discovered is it takes a mountain of time and paperwork to pull all the pieces together, followed by even more time to explain those pieces to everyone involved.

Think of this as the Super Bowl of business presentations—every detail scrutinized, every play reviewed. We say this not as an excuse, but as an explanation—and a lesson learned!

We remain committed to working with the Creditors’ Committee until we reach an agreement everyone can live with. We’re hopeful negotiations will wrap up in about a week, and we’re aiming to file a motion to adopt the plan with the bankruptcy court the week of March 11. Until then, retention and severance remains the reigning champion on our priority list.

On the bright side, for those of you in non-debtor companies (aka not in bankruptcy), new severance plans are being approved and will be rolling out soon—like a fabulous new product launch, minus the marketing blitz.

Meanwhile, we’re finalizing merit increases and promotions across the whole organization, and we’ll be sharing the good news with you next week.

And as always, we’ll continue to keep you updated on all things retention and severance. Stay tuned—same Enron time, same Enron channel!

We know how interested all of you are in the Retention & Severance Plan, so we want to update you on its status.
As many of you know, we have been working with members of the Creditors' Committee and their consultants since December to formulate a Retention & Severance Plan, and we formally presented the plan to the committee on Friday, February 22.
We had hoped the committee would approve the plan quickly so that we could file it with the bankruptcy court and share the details of the plan with you before the end of the month.
We know that many of you have career options outside of Enron and that the Retention & Severance Plan may impact your decision to stay or to leave.
We sincerely regret to inform you that approval of the plan for debtor companies is delayed.
We're learning that, in bankruptcy, most things don't move as quickly as we are accustomed.
The committee outlined some concerns related to our proposed plan, but we are confident we will be able to reach agreement with the creditors on those concerns.
The Creditors' Committee fully supports the implementation of a Retention & Severance Plan.
Such plans align the company's objectives with the goals of the creditors and are fairly standard in bankruptcy.
These plans are designed as a way to preserve and maximize value for the estate.
The Creditors' Committee also understands that time is of the essence for getting a plan in place and has established a subcommittee to expedite their review and approval process.
To that end, we are meeting regularly with the subcommittee.
We intend to work hand-in-hand with them to reach agreement on an acceptable plan as quickly as possible.
This is currently our top priority, bar none!
When we filed for bankruptcy, we did not fully grasp how tedious the process of developing an acceptable plan would be.
Unfortunately, that lack of understanding led management to set unrealistic expectations about how quickly a plan might be in place.
We now know that it takes significant time, resources and effort to understand, identify and gather the massive volume of required details, to formulate that information into a reasonable program, and to prepare a rationale and compelling presentation.
The process mirrors the most time-intensive business presentation or deal negotiation with which Enron has been involved.
That serves only as an explanation - it is not intended as an excuse.
We remain committed to working with the Creditors' Committee until we can reach agreement on a plan.
We anticipate that negotiation process will take another week or so, and have targeted the week of March 11 to file a motion to adopt a plan with the bankruptcy court.
We will continue to hold retention and severance as our number one priority until a plan is approved by the bankruptcy court.
With respect to non-debtor companies, or those companies not in bankruptcy, new severance plans are being approved and will be rolled out to employees in those companies in the very near future.
In the meantime, we have been working to finalize merit increases and promotions across the entire organization and plan to communicate those to employees next week.
And of course, we will update you on retention and severance as soon as possible.

Known as the Nigerian-419 fraud for violating section 419 of Nigerian law, these deceptive communications are sent in countless variations via surface mail, airmail, fax, and email. Employees must understand that providing *any* information will immediately compromise their financial security. Last week, I distributed a presentation that the Brattle Group gave before  the California Inquisition (i.e., legislative gas oversight committee looking  into the gas price spikes at the Cal border).
The Brattle Group is a consulting firm that Edison has long used to beat up  on SoCalGas (recall that Edison used to be a big gas customer when it owned  power plants).
Edison "arranged" for the Brattle Group to be the star  witness at the Cal Leg gas hearing.
Their job was to set up El Paso and  Dynegy for the hit at hearings that took place the following day.
Their  message was simple (and simplistic):  El Paso and Dynegy have market power.
They have used the market power to drive up basis and thus the price of gas  at the border (to "obscene" levels).
That, in turn, has driven up electricity prices.
Ken Lay is giving a gas talk tomorrow, and Rob Bradley asked that I provide  the alternative view to the Edison/Brattle rant, in the event that he gets  any questions on the topic.
It's attached.
Apologies, it's quick and dirty,  but it provides the basics.
Obviously no need for us to defend El Paso or Dynegy, but might be useful to  offer a more rationale explanation than the one that the California  Legislature is peddling.
Finally, we were also fingered somewhat as culprits at the hearing (the  California PUC FERC lawyer claimed that ENA and TW colluded to drive up basis  when ENA controlled a portion of  the capacity), but the overriding goal of  the hearing was to go after EP and Dynegy.
Best,

Subject: Review: Morgan Stanley Currency Swap Activity on EnronOnline

Team,

This email provides a concise overview of Morgan Stanley's engagement in currency swap transactions conducted via EnronOnline.

Morgan Stanley was a significant counterparty and active participant on EnronOnline, Enron's innovative electronic trading platform launched in late 1999. Beyond the widely discussed energy and commodity derivatives, Morgan Stanley regularly utilized EnronOnline for a variety of financial instruments, including currency swaps.

These currency swaps typically involved agreements between Morgan Stanley and Enron to exchange specific amounts of different currencies at a pre-agreed exchange rate on a specified future date. Such transactions were generally employed for hedging foreign exchange risk, managing international cash flows, or for speculative purposes.

EnronOnline facilitated the efficient execution and settlement of these over-the-counter (OTC) derivatives, providing real-time pricing and liquidity in a then-novel online environment. Morgan Stanley's involvement underscored the platform's reach beyond its core energy market into broader financial instruments.

Please let me know if you require further details or analysis on this particular aspect of our historical trading activities with Enron.

Best regards,

Can there not be an argument made to dive into TXN?
It's trading at 25 forward P/E (2001) with a 5-year consensus growth rate of 24.2.
A PEG of ~1 on a high quality stock with superior technology, good management, great market position and tremendous long-term growth has got to be an opportunity, right?
What's your view?
The technicals (MACD) are not great right now but I think fundamentally this is a tremendous value long-term.
It looks like the economy has really hit the brakes now (too much) but wouldn't you expect the market to begin pricing in rate cuts in 2001 pretty soon and an eventual return to high growth in technology?
I wouldn't touch any peripheral players but some of the megacap stocks with great market positions, like TXN, are sure tempting.
Nasdaq down 46% from its March high and not looking good at the open.
This could be a "buy when others are fearful" opportunity.

Subject: Assembly Considers Sweeping Bill to Restructure Power Purchases and Utility Debt Recovery

Dear Stakeholders,

The State Assembly is currently reviewing comprehensive legislation that would fundamentally alter how utilities procure power and recover outstanding debts from consumers. The proposed bill, introduced last week, aims to address mounting concerns over rising energy costs and utility company financial stability.

Key provisions under consideration include:

• Mandatory competitive bidding for all power purchase agreements exceeding $50 million annually
• Establishment of a state oversight committee to review utility debt collection practices  
• Implementation of income-based payment plans for residential customers facing financial hardship
• Restructuring of regulatory approval processes for utility rate adjustments
• Creation of a consumer protection fund financed through utility contributions

The legislation has garnered support from consumer advocacy groups while facing opposition from major utility companies, who argue the changes could undermine grid reliability and discourage infrastructure investment. Public hearings are scheduled for next month, with a committee vote expected before the legislative session ends.

We will continue monitoring this development and provide updates as the bill progresses through the legislative process. Please contact our office with any questions or concerns.

Best regards,
Policy Analysis Team

Subject: Q3 Earnings Meet Estimates with 26% Growth; Enhanced Business Unit Reporting and One-Time Charges Announced

Dear Team,

We are pleased to announce that our Q3 earnings have met market estimates, achieving a strong 26% year-over-year growth. This robust performance reflects our continued momentum across key segments and our commitment to delivering value to our stakeholders.

As part of our strategic initiative to provide greater transparency and insight into our operations, we are enhancing our business unit reporting. Beginning this quarter, we will introduce more granular segment disclosures, offering better clarity into unit performance and growth drivers.

Additionally, Q3 results include certain one-time charges largely related to our restructuring initiatives and recent investments in technology upgrades. These charges, while non-recurring, position us for greater efficiency and long-term success.

Thank you for your continued hard work and dedication. Please join our upcoming earnings call for a detailed discussion and Q&A session.

Best regards,  
[Your Name]  
[Your Position]
source_text:
Today, we announced our third quarter earnings results, which were right on target with analysts estimates for recurring earnings per diluted share of $0.43.
This marks a 26 percent increase over the third quarter of last year, which is due to the strong performance of our core wholesale and retail energy businesses and our natural gas pipelines.
In addition, we also announced that we are on track for our earnings target of $0.45 for the fourth quarter ($1.80 for 2001) and $2.15 for 2002.
We made a commitment to you that we would provide you with timely information about Enron's business strategy and performance, so this email is intended to provide an explanation about our earnings this quarter.
Over the past few months, we have met with analysts to discuss Enron's performance.
We received considerable feedback from investors and analysts that we needed to expand our financial reporting to include details for more of our business units.
In response to that feedback, we have provided results separately for several of our business units.
For example, while we have provided volume figures for North America and Europe, this is the first quarter we have provided financials separately for Enron Americas and for Europe and Other Commodities.
In addition, information about our global assets had previously been included in our numbers for Wholesale Services.
This quarter they are reported separately.
Finally, even though our broadband business is now part of Enron Wholesale Services, we are continuing to report that business separately.
Following are the highlights of our businesses:  Wholesale Services: Total income before interest, minority interests and taxes (IBIT) increased 28% to $754 million in the third quarter.
Total wholesale physical volumes increased 65% to 88.2 trillion British thermal units equivalent per day (Tbtue/d).
Americas: IBIT increased 31% to $701 million.
Natural gas volumes increased 6% to 26.7 Tbtu/d, and power volumes increased 77% to 290 million megawatt hours (MWh).
Europe and Other Commodity Markets: IBIT remained unchanged at $53 million as compared to last year.
While physical gas and power volumes increased, low volatility in these markets caused profitability to remain flat.
Retail Services: Enron Energy Services reported IBIT of $71 million, compared to $27 million a year ago.
So far this year, EES has completed more than 50 transactions with large customers and more than 95,000 deals with small business customers.
Transportation and Distribution: 	Natural Gas Pipelines: IBIT increased slightly to $85 million in the third quarter.
Portland General: We reported an IBIT loss of $(17) million this quarter compared to IBIT of $74 million a year ago.
This loss is due to power contracts PGE entered into at prices that were significantly higher than actual settled prices during the third quarter.
Last week, we  announced an agreement to sell PGE to Northwest Natural.
This transaction is expected to close next year.
Global Assets: This segment includes Elektro, Dabhol, TGS, Azurix and Enron Wind.
Third quarter IBIT remained unchanged at $19 million compared to last year.
Broadband Services: IBIT losses were $(80) million in the current quarter compared to a $(20) million loss last year.
This quarter's results include significantly lower investment-related income and lower operating costs.
Corporate and other: This segment includes the unallocated expenses associated with general corporate functions.
This segment reported an IBIT loss of $(59) million compared to $(106) million a year ago.
In addition, this quarter we announced one-time charges of $1.01 billion.
Over the past few quarters, we have conducted a thorough  review of our businesses and have decided to take certain charges to clear away issues that have clouded the performance and earnings potential  of our core businesses.
These charges include: ?
A $287 million write-down of Azurix Corp. ?
$183 million associated with the restructuring of Broadband Services.
This includes severance costs, a loss on the sale of inventory like servers and routers, and a write-down of the value of our content services contracts due to the bankruptcy of a number of customers.
?
$544 million related to losses from certain investments, primarily Enron's interest in The New Power Company, broadband and technology investments and early termination of a structured finance arrangement.
With our announcements this quarter we accomplished three things:  1) we showed continued strong earnings and earnings growth in our core businesses, 2) we cleared away those things that were clouding this superb performance in our core businesses, and 3) We expanded our reporting of financial results to increase transparency for our investors.
To read the full earnings press release, go to www.enron.com/corp/pressroom/releases.

I am writing to express my interest in joining the strategic planning and reorganization team addressing Enron's current situation. Whether your goal is to salvage the company or attract buyers, I am confident that I can add significant value to this effort.

Here are some highlights of my qualifications:
- I have experience as a "Big 5" consultant.
- I excel at identifying actionable recommendations that may have been overlooked during previous analyses.
- My background includes working across a variety of industries, where I have quickly learned the ropes and delivered results.
- While earning my graduate degree, I gained real-world experience and developed a strong, practical skill set.
- I am not a "yes" man—I value candor and integrity over empty flattery.

HOUSTON (AP) - After Enron Corp. tapped into more than $3 billion in credit in an effort to boost confidence of investors and customers, stock prices dropped.
Enron Corp.'s stock price hit its lowest point in more than five years Friday.
Shares fell 95 cents on Friday to $15.40, a level not seen since 1995, as analysts continued to muddle through a complicated series of bookkeeping issues revealed after the company's earnings announcement earlier this month.
The stock is down more than 50 percent in two weeks, and the company lost almost $14 billion in market value.
Late this week the company decided to convert $3 billion in revolving credit it has through various banks into cash.
The company put about $1.1 billion in the bank in an effort to reassure business partners and investors of its liquidity and is using the $2.2 billion balance to begin an orderly repurchase of a certain kind of short-term corporate IOU known as commercial paper.
"Nothing spells confidence quite like cash, which is what we want investors to understand," said Enron spokesman Mark Palmer of the $1.1 billion banked this week.
Palmer could neither confirm nor deny that the company is negotiating further lines of credit with banks but described such actions as "good management decisions."
On Oct. 16 Enron's third-quarter earnings release drew renewed attention to an issue investors and analysts had previously been unhappy about: Then-Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow, with the Enron board's approval, had formed and run two investment partnerships that could have created a conflict of interest.
The partnerships, LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, did complex financing and hedging deals with Enron.
Fastow had resigned from his roles in the partnerships months ago when Wall Street began to question whether he could watch out for the interests of Enron's shareholders and the investment partnership simultaneously.
But last week when the company reported a $35 million loss related to ending its LJM ties as well as a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, new questions began to arise.
The Securities and Exchange Commission's Division of Enforcement launched an informal inquiry into the partnerships, and earlier this week Fastow was put on a leave of absence.
Reducing the company's debt exposure through commercial paper and putting it back into more traditional financial tools, like a revolving line of credit, could give great peace of mind to Enron's investors, said Anatol Feygin, an analyst with J.P. Morgan.
"It helps them shore up their support behind their energy trading business, which is really the core of their operations," Feygin told the Houston Chronicle for Saturday's editions.
Carol Coale, an analyst with Prudential Securities, still sees the move as somewhat confusing.
"Just last week they were touting their unused lines of credit as a plus, but the fact that they tapped those now sends a strange, mixed message," she said.
"Do they need the cash to keep the rating agencies off their back?
Is it a gesture for customers?
It first struck me as another one of these strangely timed actions on the part of management."

February 4, 2002 Enron boss cancels testimony  Cites 'disturbing' TV talk: Blames 'prosecutorial' tone, claims of security fraud Jason Chow  National Post  Former Enron Corp. chairman Kenneth Lay said yesterday he would not testify at today's scheduled congressional hearing into the company's collapse, blaming legislators' "prosecutorial" comments on TV talk shows yesterday.

"Not only were there corrupt practices, we are finding what may clearly end up being security fraud," Republican Rep. Billy Tauzin, chairman of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, told NBC's Meet the Press. Tauzin specifically cited executives' alleged use of off-the-books partnerships, such as the now-infamous LJM and Chewco entities, to conceal massive debt and inflate earnings, misleading both investors and employees about Enron’s true financial health.

An internal company report released Saturday criticized Mr. Lay, other executives, board members and auditors for the collapse. The report, commissioned by a special committee of Enron's board and led by William Powers, dean of the University of Texas Law School, detailed how senior managers, including CFO Andrew Fastow, created and exploited complex partnerships to enrich themselves and manipulate the company’s reported profits. It showed managers took home millions of dollars through these partnerships—Fastow alone reportedly pocketed more than US$30-million personally—while hiding at least US$1-billion in losses through these entities.

Other politicians denounced the company's management before TV cameras yesterday in response to the report. For example, Sen. Carl Levin (D-Mich.) called Enron's accounting practices “a willful deception” and Rep. Henry Waxman (D-Calif.) accused top executives of lying to Congress when they previously testified about the company’s finances.

Last night, Mr. Lay cancelled his testimony.

"In the midst of our preparation, particularly disturbing statements have been made by members of Congress, even today, on the eve of Mr. Lay's scheduled appearance," his lawyer, Earl Silbert, said in a letter to lawmakers on the Senate Commerce Committee and the House Financial Services Committee. Silbert specifically cited televised remarks suggesting criminal culpability against Mr. Lay before he had the opportunity to present his side.

"I have instructed Mr. Lay to withdraw his prior acceptance of your invitation."

Sen. Byron Dorgan, chairman of another Senate Commerce subcommittee investigating the biggest bankruptcy in U.S. history, said on Meet the Press the report "suggests massive problems" and shows "a culture of corruption." Dorgan pointed to internal emails revealed in the report showing that company officials were warned by employees about accounting irregularities but dismissed or ignored such concerns.

While Mr. Dorgan said it was up to the U.S. Justice Department to decide whether to press criminal charges, he added the report showed "clearly some things have happened here that are going to put some people here in real jeopardy." He highlighted, for instance, how thousands of Enron employees lost their jobs and life savings, while executives cashed in tens of millions in stock options.

The 203-page report, written by a team headed by the dean of the University of Texas Law School, said Mr. Lay "bears significant responsibility" for "flawed decisions" in approving some transactions that hid debt and offset losses. The report catalogued Lay’s role in signing off on key deals, including the Raptors and LJM partnerships, despite internal warnings from finance executives and outside consultants that these transactions were high-risk and could jeopardize the company’s stability.

The report said these transactions did not follow accounting rules and were implemented improperly, resulting in Enron overstating earnings by US$1-billion during a one-year period starting in September, 2000. Specifically, the powers report described how Enron would move poorly performing assets into special-purpose entities and record fictional profits from transactions with these same entities, creating the illusion of growth while hiding steep losses from company shareholders and federal regulators.

"Ken Lay obviously had to know that this was a giant pyramid scheme -- a giant shell game," said Republican Sen. Peter Fitzgerald. He added that Lay, as the company’s longtime chief executive and chairman, participated in board meetings where the partnerships and deals at the heart of Enron’s manipulation were discussed, making claims of ignorance unlikely.

On Saturday, June 9, Tropical Storm Allison's relentless winds and torrential downpours left Houston in chaos, dumping more than 20 inches of rain and flooding the city's streets, highways, and neighborhoods in a matter of hours. Cars sat submerged on major freeways, families were trapped on rooftops, and rescue boats navigated what had been busy intersections just hours before.

As of Sunday night, 17 people had died in the storm and many others are still missing.

One of those who perished in the fatal flood was one of our employees, a summer intern in ETS and student at Texas A & M University, Chad Garren.

Our condolences go out to his family and co-workers.

At this time, Enron Community Relations and Aggies@Enron <mailto:Aggies@Enron> are planning to establish a scholarship fund in his memory.

More information on the fund will be forthcoming.

Enron has made a corporate contribution of $500,000 to the American Red Cross to aid in the victim relief effort.

Enron employees are encouraged to donate to relief efforts and to take advantage of our Matching Gift Program to double the impact of your individual donation.

Enron will match your contribution dollar for dollar and your donation will not be counted against your $15,000 annual limit.

Although Enron is supporting the American Red Cross, please feel free to make your donation to the non-profit organization of your choice that is offering aid to flood victims (they must provide proof of their 501c 3 status).

Please send your check to EB1635a before Friday, June 15, and we will send it, along with a matching check to the appropriate agency.

On the memo line of your check, please make sure to write "Houston Flood Relief."

We know that many Enron employees have been severely impacted by this devastating flood - homes have been destroyed, belongings lost, and families forced to evacuate with only the clothes on their backs.

Enron cares about you and your family and would like to make sure that your immediate needs are being met.

If you have been displaced because of the flood, please contact the Community Relations hotline at ext. 37181 for assistance.

Also, if you would like to help your co-workers who have been displaced, an account has been set up at the Enron Federal Credit Union to accept donations.

Please bring/send your contribution to the Enron Federal Credit Union and make your checks out to Employee Flood Relief.

There are many agencies in Houston in need of volunteer assistance - from sandbagging operations to shelter coordination to meal preparation for displaced families.

If you would like to volunteer, please e-mail your name and extension to communityrelations@enron.com <mailto:communityrelations@enron.com>.

Please note if you are willing to lead a project.

Again, our hearts go out to Chad's family and to all of you who have been impacted by this tragedy.

Please continue to watch your e-mail for more information.

Sovereign Bond Spreads: Significant New Issuance - CSFB Commentary: The emerging debt markets rallied the week ending August 3, 2001, as the long expected new US$8 billion IMF package for Argentina was finally announced on Tuesday, July 31, 2001.
Argentina will receive US$8bn in new loans from the IMF, of which US$5bn will be allocated next month (August 2001) to reinforce reserves that were depleted as a result of massive savings withdrawal.
Another US$3bn will be extended if Argentina obtains an agreement to cut financing costs through a debt swap and possible buyback.
The rally in Argentina spilled over first to the higher yielding EM assets (Brazil, Turkey, and others), then helped other credits, although the impact was softer.
However, the Argentine problem is far from solved, as Argentina's government still has to deliver on its promises of its 'Deficit Zero' policy and debt restructuring; therefore, the medium-term outlook is still cautious.
The Turkish market traded up after the Argentina package was announced; the rally was also helped by satisfactory T-Bills auction results and other positive news from the country.
For Russian assets, the IMF announcement was also a long awaited boost: volumes increased significantly with prices climbing by more than 2 points in price.
The Russian US$ yield curve is getting very steep because most of the supply that we see is concentrated in Russia 2030, while the buying interest is spread across the curve.
Central and Eastern European asset prices were on average ? point higher on the week, with Poland underperforming other countries after S&P changed its outlook on Poland's long-term foreign currency rating from "positive" to "stable".
The EMBI+ Index tightened by 50 bps in one session on Wednesday, August 1, 2001, and closed 29 bps tighter on the week.

On Tuesday, July 31, 2001, the FOMC cut the Fed Funds rate for the 7th time this year by 25 bps to 3.50%, the lowest since April 1994.
The accompanying Fed statement pointed at the slowing global growth and weakening business profits and capital spending in the US, thus suggesting further easing is possible.

As market conditions remain difficult and we are still in a traditional August holiday period, primary market activity is very slow but expected to soar in September with a number of deals waiting in the pipeline.

Sue: Sorry that I didn't get back to you over the weekend but with Arthur's baseball schedule and all the running around that we were trying to do, things were a bit hectic.

I'm officially brain dead today so I thought that I would take a break and write to one of my favorite people.

Things on the baby front are progressing well. On our last ultrasound we got the news that we were hoping for with respect to the placenta problem and so I've got the green light basically to do whatever I want to do although I am still taking it easy and swimming a lot. The baby weighed about 4 pounds a few weeks ago and everything looked great so I was quite relieved. Now I'm trying to spend what little free time I have getting ready. The people here at work are having a baby shower a week from Friday so hopefully that will help since other than some of Arthur's clothes I am starting from scratch.

Work is going well although I am looking forward to winding down in a few weeks. I'm hoping that I can work up until the very end to maximize my time off but we will see how that goes. I really feel great except for being uncomfortable at night and not getting much sleep but I suppose that this is good practice for when the baby comes.

Arthur is doing great. We got him 2 gerbils as a substitute for a larger pet! They're pretty cute, small, clean and so far easy to maintain. He is still heavily into baseball and was just selected for the All-star team which we were absolutely thrilled about as was he! He called dad practically every day that he was trying out for the team to give him an update and I'm hoping that dad can fly down for the tournament this weekend. Arthur would be on cloud nine if he came. We'll see.

Speaking of hectic weekends, something funny happened last Saturday after Arthur’s game. As we were leaving the field, Arthur accidentally left his glove behind on the bleachers. We didn’t notice until we were halfway home and he was nearly in tears, worried someone else might take his “lucky glove.” So, spur of the moment, we drove all the way back, only to discover a group of little kids using his glove to scoop up popcorn and throw it in the air for the birds! Arthur (after a moment of horror) ended up laughing with them and joining in, and before we knew it, all the kids had invented a popcorn-tossing contest right there on the grass. He even made a new friend from another team, and they traded baseball cards afterward. It was such a sweet reminder that sometimes, the little mishaps become the happiest memories.

Mom and dad offered to keep Arthur for a week over the summer and we are looking into that. I'm toying with the possibility of sending him when the baby is born, but I'll just have to see how it works out. I would really love for you and mom to come once the baby is born. Do you have any thoughts on that? You are obviously welcome at any time, but I sense from mom that she would prefer to wait until sometime in August. Let me know what you think.

How is Cindy doing? Do you know what she needs for her new addition? Do you want to get her a joint gift? Let me know. I'm happy to do either something on my own or jointly with you.

How's Cate? Give her my best. What's new with you and your career situation? I hope that you are enjoying what you are doing. I certainly am and I am still undecided about what I am going to do once the baby is born, although I would really like to take the rest of the year off.

I've got to run to my "baby class" tonight. Take care and I will try to catch up with you sometime. I love you!

Carol

Leveraging existing investments such as ERP into new arenas will be critical in assuring maximum value is delivered.""
A panel of senior technology officers, including Xavier Flinois, president, Schlumberger Network Solutions; Tom Halbouty, CIO, Pioneer Natural Resources; Paul Cuneo, CIO, Equiva Services LLP; and Ray Cline, CTO, SAIC, will follow Amidei's presentation.

Accenture Partner Jeff Sakaguchi will direct the discussion.

Will Symmes, director - energy information systems, will describe how Reliant has developed an internet-based energy information and analysis portal for large industrial customers, entitled "Energy Commander."

Subject: Enhancing Deal Valuation and Pricing with the EES Model

Dear [Recipient Name],

I hope this email finds you well.

I wanted to share some insights on an advanced analytical framework that is proving highly effective in today's complex M&A landscape: the EES model for deal valuation and pricing.

The EES model represents a sophisticated approach designed to move beyond traditional financial metrics, offering a more comprehensive and dynamic understanding of a deal's true value. It integrates a broader spectrum of critical factors, including:

*   **Economic Drivers:** Analyzing macro and microeconomic conditions, industry trends, and their specific impact on the target and combined entity.
*   **Ecosystem Dynamics:** Assessing the competitive landscape, supply chain resilience, regulatory environment, and stakeholder relationships.
*   **Scenario Planning:** Building robust models that evaluate valuation and pricing across various future scenarios, accounting for market shifts, operational synergies, and potential risks.

**Key Benefits for Deal Valuation and Pricing:**

1.  **Holistic Perspective:** Provides a 360-degree view, ensuring all value drivers and potential detractors are considered, not just historical financials.
2.  **Enhanced Accuracy & Defensibility:** Leads to more robust and justifiable valuations, critical for successful negotiations and stakeholder buy-in.
3.  **Strategic Insight:** Uncovers opportunities for long-term value creation, competitive advantage, and synergy realization that might be overlooked by standard models.
4.  **Optimized Pricing Strategies:** Enables more precise and data-driven pricing, ensuring deals are structured to maximize returns while mitigating risk.
5.  **Improved Risk Mitigation:** Identifies potential vulnerabilities and allows for proactive planning to protect value.

By leveraging the EES model, organizations can achieve superior deal outcomes, make more informed investment decisions, and ensure their pricing strategies are both aggressive and sustainable.

I would be delighted to arrange a brief call to discuss how the EES model could be tailored to your specific deal valuation and pricing needs. Please let me know your availability.

Best regards,

[Your Name]
[Your Title]
[Your Company]
[Your Contact Information]

I read Wednesday's NGPL order (RP00-18-002) as applying only to NGPL due to  their unique restrictions and tariff rules.
I do not read it as forcing the  rest of the industry (i.e., us) to use the floor rate as the reserve price  for negotiated index rate bids and ordinary recourse rate bids.
I think we  can still determine the reserve price on a prearranged deal like the ENA deal  based on our good faith valuation of the upside provided by the index  mechanism.
I.e., on that type of deal, we can determine that the index  mechanism is worth "x cents" to us and require a discounted recourse rate  bidder to bid more than the floor plus x cents to win.
Agreed?
Note that NGPL whined that the unique rules they are subject to place them at  a competitve disadvantage to the rest of the industry (i.e., us) on this  issue.
The commission didn't say anything about that, implying to me that  the rest of us are still free to do what NGPL cannot do.
DF

text: Dave, I still believe the most flexible model, offering high ROCE and growth unconstrained by capital, is the one Enron employs. I think the cash-on-cash returns on these Gencos in the short run will be good; however, it will be difficult for these companies to move quickly to react to market opportunities given their need to protect their long position (not unlike our friends in the oil & gas producing sector). It is not a bad model, just a different one. Either way, they will be strong bidders for assets given their story to Wall Street. Regards

Provided herewith is a complete copy of the California Public Utilities Commission's (CPUC) Order on Southern California Gas Company's (SoCalGas) Rate Schedule for Large Service (RLS) Tariff for peaking rates applicable to bypass customers.

Significant deviations are observed in the final order compared to the previously issued proposed decision, specifically regarding the incorporation of an interruptible rate.

The Order comprises the following key provisions:
1. Two distinct rates were adopted: a firm cost-based peaking rate and an interruptible peaking rate.
2. The firm cost-based peaking rate shall incorporate the following components:
    a. A monthly customer charge, designed to recover the costs associated with customer-related facilities. The precise rate shall be contingent upon customer classification, ranging from $800 to $19,000.
    b. A volumetric Public Purpose Program surcharge, calculated in accordance with Commission-approved rates.
    c. A monthly reservation rate, determined by multiplying the currently authorized end-use customer class rate by the Maximum Daily Quantity (MDQ).
3. The interruptible peaking rate is established at 150% of SoCalGas' default tariff rate, assuming a 100% load factor.
4. Firm and interruptible customers shall be subject to a volumetric rate designed to recover the Interstate Transition Cost Surcharge, the Sempra system-wide rate charge, and any other analogous surcharges.
5. Additional provisions stipulate that customers shall be subject to daily balancing requirements, interruptible customers are ineligible for Service Interruption Credits, and the tariff's application shall be on a facility-by-facility basis.

SoCalGas was directed to file modified cost-based tariff sheets within ten (10) days of the issuance of the Order (due August 12, 2001).

Should you require further clarification or have any inquiries, please do not hesitate to contact the undersigned.

Dear Ken,

I would like to thank you for the great experience that I had with Enron, and for the opportunity that you gave me three years ago. I joined Enron looking for a change and I have never regretted my choice.

A lot of things changed over this time. In my first presentation to Gazprom in Moscow, I remember, that I pictured Enron as the largest gas pipeline operator in Americas aggressively looking for energy development projects in emerging markets. Two years later, I was talking to Microsoft executives in Redmond, who were looking for a partner to conquer a high-tech broadband world. I don't know any other company, which can offer such an opportunity for a change and growth, and which is able to change itself so much as Enron.

I am grateful that over this time you have been personally involved in my business career and introduced me to the Enron management team - Mark Frevert, Richard DiMichele, Vince Kaminsky and others. I also would like to use this opportunity to admit some of my mistakes. As it was my first experience inside a corporate environment (not as CEO), it took me some time to develop relationships with people inside Enron. These relationships are critical to achieving success within the company. But Enron is a great place to learn, and in a culture that encourages innovation and risk-taking, some mistakes are inevitable.

I am pleased that the deal that my team and I developed and managed to provide Microsoft (MSN) with broadband network was successful (you may remember we discussed this idea prior to my move to Enron Broadband Services). This spring I took advantage of your recommendation and graduated from the Harvard Advanced Management Program. It was a great experience and I learned professionally and personally. It was a very competitive group of executives from all over the world, and the program consisted of a three-month intensive academic curriculum. Together with one of my Harvard classmates and his Canadian telecom company, we are now working to start a new business in the US.

You have a challenging task to return Enron to its leadership position. I admire the steps that you are making. Without restoring integrity to internal and external relationships, it would be impossible to achieve this goal. I have no doubts that you and your colleagues will make this happen.

I wish you all the best and thank you again for the opportunity that you gave me.

Enron Draws on $3 Billion Credit Line as Stock Plummets  
10/27/2001 Associated Press Newswires (Copyright 2001. The Associated Press. All Rights Reserved.)

HOUSTON (AP) — In a bid to reassure investors and business partners, Enron Corp. accessed more than $3 billion in credit this week. Despite the move, the company’s stock continued to tumble, closing Friday at $15.40 — its lowest level in over five years and a drop of 95 cents for the day. The share price, now at a level not seen since 1995, has plunged by more than 50 percent in just two weeks, erasing nearly $14 billion in market value.

To bolster its financial position, Enron converted $3 billion from its revolving credit facilities into cash, depositing about $1.1 billion to underscore its liquidity. The company is using the remaining $2.2 billion to begin an orderly repurchase of its commercial paper, a form of short-term corporate debt. 

"Nothing spells confidence quite like cash, which is what we want investors to understand," said company spokesman Mark Palmer.

Palmer declined to comment on whether Enron is in talks to secure additional credit lines, but called such measures “good management decisions.”

Enron’s financial troubles intensified after an October 16 earnings release drew renewed scrutiny to controversial partnerships established by then-CFO Andrew Fastow, with the board’s approval. The two entities, LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, engaged in complex deals with Enron and raised conflict of interest concerns. Fastow had resigned from the partnerships months earlier amid mounting pressure from Wall Street.

Last week, Enron reported a $35 million loss from ending its LJM relationships and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, sparking fresh questions and prompting the SEC to launch an informal inquiry into the transactions. Fastow was placed on leave earlier this week in hopes of restoring investor confidence.

J.P. Morgan analyst Anatol Feygin said Enron's shift from commercial paper to traditional credit lines could reassure investors and bolster the core energy trading business. "It helps them shore up their support behind their energy trading business, which is really the core of their operations," Feygin told the Houston Chronicle.

HOUSTON (AP) - After Enron Corp. tapped into more than $3 billion in credit in an effort to boost confidence of investors and customers, stock prices dropped.
Enron Corp.'s stock price hit its lowest point in more than five years Friday.
Shares fell 95 cents on Friday to $15.40, a level not seen since 1995, as analysts continued to muddle through a complicated series of bookkeeping issues revealed after the company's earnings announcement earlier this month.
The stock is down more than 50 percent in two weeks, and the company lost almost $14 billion in market value.
Late this week the company decided to convert $3 billion in revolving credit it has through various banks into cash.
The company put about $1.1 billion in the bank in an effort to reassure business partners and investors of its liquidity and is using the $2.2 billion balance to begin an orderly repurchase of a certain kind of short-term corporate IOU known as commercial paper.
"Nothing spells confidence quite like cash, which is what we want investors to understand," said Enron spokesman Mark Palmer of the $1.1 billion banked this week.
Palmer could neither confirm nor deny that the company is negotiating further lines of credit with banks but described such actions as "good management decisions."
On Oct. 16 Enron's third-quarter earnings release drew renewed attention to an issue investors and analysts had previously been unhappy about: Then-Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow, with the Enron board's approval, had formed and run two investment partnerships that could have created a conflict of interest.
The partnerships, LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, did complex financing and hedging deals with Enron.
Fastow had resigned from his roles in the partnerships months ago when Wall Street began to question whether he could watch out for the interests of Enron's shareholders and the investment partnership simultaneously.
But last week when the company reported a $35 million loss related to ending its LJM ties as well as a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, new questions began to arise.
The Securities and Exchange Commission's Division of Enforcement launched an informal inquiry into the partnerships, and earlier this week Fastow was put on a leave of absence.
Reducing the company's debt exposure through commercial paper and putting it back into more traditional financial tools, like a revolving line of credit, could give great peace of mind to Enron's investors, said Anatol Feygin, an analyst with J.P. Morgan.
"It helps them shore up their support behind their energy trading business, which is really the core of their operations," Feygin told the Houston Chronicle for Saturday's editions.
Carol Coale, an analyst with Prudential Securities, still sees the move as somewhat confusing.
"Just last week they were touting their unused lines of credit as a plus, but the fact that they tapped those now sends a strange, mixed message," she said.
"Do they need the cash to keep the rating agencies off their back?
Is it a gesture for customers?
It first struck me as another one of these strangely timed actions on the part of management."

Subject: Accounting Treatment for Potential Lease Agreement with USTeleNetRespond

Dear [Recipient Name],

I am writing to outline the accounting treatment considerations for the potential lease agreement with USTeleNetRespond. Under ASC 842 (Leases), we will need to assess whether the arrangement contains a lease and, if so, classify it as either an operating or finance lease based on the contract terms.

If the agreement grants us the right to control the use of identified property, plant, or equipment for a period in exchange for consideration, we will recognize a right-of-use asset and a corresponding lease liability at commencement. The liability will be measured at the present value of lease payments, and the asset will include the initial measurement of the liability plus any prepaid lease payments and direct costs.

For an operating lease, lease expense will be recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term. For a finance lease, we will recognize interest expense on the liability and amortization of the right-of-use asset separately. Additional disclosures and ongoing reassessments may be required as details are finalized.

Please let me know if you need a more detailed analysis once the agreement terms are available.

Best regards,  
[Your Name]

Just to follow-up on our discussion yesterday regarding the accounting treatment assuming that USTeleNet owns the switch and that we purchase the switch and lease it back to them under a "capital" lease, the following would occur:  The asset would stay on their books (however it would be "marked-up" to FMV as evidenced by the purchase price) They would defer the gain, if any, over the asset's life.
They would record a payable on their balance sheet and recognize interest expense in their P&L as payments are made We would record the payment of cash to them and book a receivable and deferred interest income (to be recognized over the lease term)  Essentially we are lending them money equal to the FMV of their asset and receiving interest payments in return (i.e.

Ted Murphy and I met with the Arthur Andersen team this morning that accompanied us on our comprehensive three-day trip to Buenos Aires last week. The AA team consisted of senior partners John Richardson and Maria Santos, along with risk management specialists David Chen and Patricia Williams, who conducted extensive interviews with over fifteen local staff members and reviewed our operational procedures across all departments.

We thoroughly reviewed the detailed observations and recommendations in written form that we had discussed briefly with you on our last day in your office. The document spans twelve pages and covers critical areas including operational risk controls, regulatory compliance with Argentine financial laws, foreign exchange hedging procedures, credit risk management protocols, and staff training requirements. The team identified several gaps in our current control framework, particularly in the areas of trade confirmation processes and daily mark-to-market procedures, which could expose us to significant operational losses if not addressed promptly.

After making a few substantive changes based on our discussion, including modifications to the recommended timeline for implementation and adjustments to the proposed staffing levels, AA should be forwarding to you a copy of the draft document later this afternoon via secure email transmission. The revised recommendations now include a phased approach to implementing new controls over the next six months, with priority given to the most critical risk areas identified during our assessment.

We would welcome your detailed comments and your additions on anything that you think we may have missed, particularly regarding local market practices and regulatory nuances that may not have been fully captured during our visit. Your insights into the practical challenges of implementing these recommendations in the Buenos Aires office environment would be invaluable, as would any additional observations about staff capabilities and training needs that emerged after our departure.

Ted and I will be meeting with Rick Causey and Rick Buy within the next couple of days to discuss our comprehensive operations and control review findings, present our recommendations for immediate action items, and secure approval for the necessary budget allocations to implement the proposed improvements. Your responses would be welcomed prior to that meeting, ideally by close of business tomorrow, so we can incorporate your feedback into our presentation and ensure we have a complete picture of the situation before making our formal recommendations to senior management.

I look forward to working closely with you and others in your office in my expanded role overseeing Global Risk Management Operations. This issue centers entirely on tank relocation. If a tank has been moved to another location, it triggers requirements which were enacted on the date of the relocation. Subject: Energy Market Competition: Major Challenges and Setbacks in 2001

Dear Colleagues,

I hope this message finds you well. As we reflect on the significant developments in energy markets during 2001, I wanted to share some thoughts on the major challenges and setbacks that have reshaped our industry landscape.

**California Electricity Crisis**

The California electricity crisis reached its peak in early 2001, fundamentally challenging assumptions about deregulated energy markets. Rolling blackouts affected millions of customers, wholesale electricity prices soared to unprecedented levels, and Pacific Gas & Electric filed for bankruptcy protection. The crisis exposed critical flaws in market design, including inadequate supply capacity, transmission constraints, and regulatory gaps that allowed for market manipulation. This situation has prompted serious reconsideration of deregulation models nationwide and highlighted the importance of maintaining adequate reserve margins and robust oversight mechanisms.

**Enron's Collapse**

The bankruptcy filing of Enron Corporation in December 2001 sent shockwaves throughout the energy sector and financial markets. Once hailed as an innovative leader in energy trading and marketing, Enron's collapse revealed massive accounting fraud and raised serious questions about corporate governance, risk management, and regulatory oversight in competitive energy markets. The company's failure has undermined confidence in energy trading operations and prompted increased scrutiny of mark-to-market accounting practices and off-balance-sheet transactions across the industry.

**September 11th Impact**

The tragic events of September 11th created immediate disruptions in energy markets and heightened concerns about infrastructure security. Oil and natural gas prices experienced significant volatility, energy trading floors were evacuated, and questions arose about the vulnerability of critical energy infrastructure to potential attacks. The events have accelerated discussions about energy security, emergency preparedness, and the need for enhanced protection of power plants, pipelines, and other essential facilities.

**Looking Forward**

These events collectively represent a watershed moment for energy market competition. While the fundamental benefits of competitive markets remain valid, 2001 has demonstrated the critical importance of proper market design, effective regulation, corporate accountability, and infrastructure security. As we move forward, our industry must address these lessons learned while continuing to pursue the efficiencies and innovations that competition can provide.

I welcome your thoughts on how these developments may influence our strategic planning and risk management approaches going forward.

Best regards,

[Your name]
[Your title]
[Company name]

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL: Mike Peterson asked me to share this update with you, along with the attached order: We've attached an Order signed yesterday and entered this morning by Judge Rosenthal regarding Plaintiffs' Motion for TRO and Preliminary Injunctive Relief (which includes a request to freeze defendants' "insider trading proceeds") – that's the matter from the highly publicized hearing last month.

As you may recall, at the end of the hearing, Judge Rosenthal asked for further briefing on a rather intricate legal point: whether the Court had the authority to issue the preliminary relief requested. Both parties submitted their briefs on this on December 15 and December 21.

In the attached Order, Judge Rosenthal has concluded that the Court *does* have the necessary authority, but that the current record doesn't contain enough evidence to warrant freezing any individual defendant's proceeds from the sale of Enron stock.

You might also be pleased to know about two additional points in the Court's opinion: (a) at several places, the Court clearly indicates that any "freeze" or similar injunctive relief for any defendant would need to be based on specific, individualized evidence for that person; and (b) the Court states that plaintiffs would have to meet a very difficult "tracing" requirement to establish a right to a constructive trust or freeze (meaning they'd have to "trace" a specific asset or fund of money held by a defendant directly back to the profits of an improper insider trade).

On the flip side, the aspects of the Court's opinion that could arguably be favorable to the plaintiffs are: (a) the discussion of "an equitable accounting," where the Court suggests that the plaintiffs *might* be able to meet the requirements for an order asking defendants to account for profits earned by trading Enron securities between October 1998 and November 2001; and (b) an opportunity (until January 23) for plaintiffs to file a brief outlining any expedited discovery they believe they're entitled to regarding the individual defendants, "particularly as to . . . Kenneth Lay, Jeffrey Skilling, and Andrew Fastow."

We'll be sure to keep you updated on any further developments.
– Mike Peterson
Please don't hesitate to reach out to us if you have any questions or comments at all.
Best regards,
Terri

Subject: Chapter 11 Update: Organizational and Personnel Matters

Dear Team,

As we continue to navigate our Chapter 11 restructuring process, we want to provide you with an important update regarding our organizational structure and personnel matters.

Our overarching goal through this restructuring is to emerge as a more resilient, efficient, and strategically focused organization, well-positioned for long-term success. To achieve this, we have undertaken a thorough review of our operational framework and staffing requirements.

This review has led to necessary organizational adjustments designed to streamline our operations, enhance productivity, and align our resources with our core business objectives. These changes are crucial steps in building a sustainable future for our company.

Regarding personnel, we understand that periods of change can bring uncertainty, and we want to acknowledge the impact of these decisions on our valued employees. As part of these restructuring efforts, we have made the difficult but necessary decision to adjust our workforce in certain areas. These decisions were made after careful consideration and are essential to secure the company's future. For those whose roles have been impacted, we are providing support and resources to assist them through this transition. We extend our deepest gratitude for their contributions.

For our continuing team members, your dedication and adaptability are invaluable. We are committed to fostering a stable and supportive work environment as we move forward. We believe these organizational and personnel realignments will enable us to operate more effectively, serve our customers better, and achieve our strategic goals post-emergence.

We will continue to share updates as our Chapter 11 process progresses. Should you have any questions or require further information, please reach out to your direct manager or the Human Resources department.

Thank you for your understanding, continued hard work, and commitment to our company's future.

Sincerely,

[Your Name/Leadership Team]

As things begin to calm down somewhat after events of last week, we wanted to update all employees of certain organizational and personnel changes that have occurred recently.
Organizational Matters The Creditors' Committee was formed last week by the United States Trustee.
This committee is comprised of 15 individuals representing various creditor groups including: banks, bondholders, insurance companies and employees.
The Creditors' Committee will be the key point of contact as we reorganize the company and emerge from Chapter 11.
Initially, they will send financial advisors to our offices to monitor any asset liquidations as well as review our cash flow projections.
Ultimately, they will be responsible for approving our reorganization plan as to which assets or businesses we sell and which ones we retain.
From an Enron perspective, the plans for reorganization have already begun.
Overhead has been reduced dramatically, certain employee retention programs have been put in place and a wider retention program is currently being developed.
We hope to share the wider retention program with you in the very near future.
Furthermore, detail cash flow projections are in their final stages of preparation and will be reviewed by senior management this week.
This will be the critical first step in formulating our reorganization strategy to emerge from Chapter 11 as a healthy company.
By now, you must have heard of "NETCO."
This company was formed as a means to maximize the value of Enron's most valuable business, the wholesale energy business.
Certain Enron North America employees have been assigned to NETCO to re-build the North American gas and power business under different ownership.
We will be filing with the bankruptcy court this week proposed auction procedures to allow bidders to bid for NETCO.
It is our expectation that Enron would retain a 49 percent (or perhaps less) non-controlling interest in NETCO.
The NETCO employees would become employees of the winning bidder.
We anticipate this process to reach closure sometime in January.
As for the remaining businesses of Enron, they are all under review as to which ones will be proposed for sale and which ones will be proposed for retention.
This review process will take time as it will require approval of the Creditors' Committee.
We will update you periodically on our process.
Personnel Matters As a result of our current situation, we have made many personnel changes over the past several months to maximize the value of the organization.
Office of the Chairman - Enron Corp Jeff McMahon, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, has been added to the Office of the Chairman of Enron Corp along with Ken Lay and Greg Whalley.
Among other things, Jeff has been working on the business plan for reorganization in Chapter 11 and is the primary contact with the newly formed Creditor's Committee.
Treasurer - Enron Corp Ray Bowen was elected to Executive Vice President, Finance and Treasurer of Enron Corp recently.
In this role, Ray is responsible for all finance activities of Enron Corp.  Ray also has the lead role in managing the cash activities of the company on a day to day basis.
Corporate Development Mark Muller has been appointed Executive Vice President - Corporate Development.
In this role, Mark will work with Enron's various business units on all asset disposals, which will be a key element in Enron's reorganization plan and value preservation.
Wholesale Services The Wholesale Services group has been reorganized under the leadership of Jim Fallon.
Included in this group are the following businesses, ENA, EBS, EIM and EGM.
As part of the Chapter 11 reorganization, efforts in these businesses will be directed at maximizing value for the creditors as well as determining which businesses or assets will be part of Enron's reorganization plan.
Management Committee Departures Unfortunately, due to the current financial condition of the company, the following members of the management committee have left the company or will be leaving the company by the end of December:  Michael Brown Mark Frevert Steve Kean Mike McConnell Jeff Shankman  Additionally, John Lavorato and Louise Kitchen have resigned from the Management Committee to arrange for the joint venture energy activities of NETCO.
We know as employees the uncertainty surrounding the future of the company is unsettling.
Unfortunately, that aspect will not change in the near term.
We ask for everyone's patience and continued support as we move forward through the Chapter 11 process.
We are committed to reorganizing into a strong company once again and will need the help of all the employees to achieve that goal.

Wednesday afternoon, February 6th, 2002, the Enron building had a brief encounter with darkness—a power outage! Usually, our building is powered by not one, but two Reliant circuits (because who doesn’t like a little backup?).

Wednesday afternoon Febuary 6th, 2002, the Enron building experienced a brief power outage.
The building is powered by one of two Reliant circuits.
Yesterday, while a backup circuit was turned off for nearby construction of the light rail system, the primary circuit failed.
Typically, the backup system would have switch on immediately, but because the backup circuit was off the building's backup generators were activated creating what was perceived by some as smoke.
While there was no fire within the building, many employees quickly evacuated the building through the stairwell.
Given heighten concerns for national security, evacuation was indeed appropriate and we appreciate that employees conducted the evacuation calmly and courteously.
Enron Property & Services Corp

We  reached a conceptual agreement with the government representatives on Sunday night.
The main points are:         1.
Rationing losses:   Defined methodology giving distribution companies recovery over the next 36 months of rationing losses realised   from June 01 until the end of rationing in 02.
Recovery includes financial compensation.
Immediate funding of 80% through BNDES, with Brazilian government funds.
Loans liquidated over the 3 year period as tariff increases are realised.
Funding scheduled by December 15th.
Elektro Ebitda impact of approximately R$191million or US$ 73 million.
2.
April/May MAE settlement :   Market will settle under current rules due to pre-rationing conditions, confirming the procedures used on Elektro's books.
Impact of approximately R$ 18 million or US$ 7 million.
3.
Parcel  "A" for the future:  All non-controlable costs to which LDC's are subjected to including power purchases, sector charges, are passed through to final tariffs either using a tracking account mechanism or by aligning adjustment dates with  the LDC tariff revision date.
Tracking account will be subject to financial compensation from the date costs are incurred until the effective pass through and collection , eliminating a major risk for the distribution sector.
Elektro Ebitda impact  2002 forward of R$ 60 million or US$ 19 million, as had been considered in the 2002 plan.
This methodology represents major risk mitigation going forward, as the initial power supply contracts are renewed starting in 2003.
4.
Parcel A from the past:   Min Parente has agreed to the concept recovering non controllable  that were not passed through to tariffs since late 1999 using the same methodology agreed to for future recoveries and has a dedicated team from the Federal Attorney General's office targeting a final solution in ten days.
Elektro impact  is R$145 million or US$ 55 million in 2001.
The proposed mechanism for recovery is after the 36 months for the rationing losses.
We are currently finalising a memo of understanding and the government team is winding up the settlement with the generators in order to finalize the terms of the overall agreement.
Min Parente has committed to resolving the open issues affecting investors in the power sector.
These  agreements represent a major step forward, significantly improving  the value of our businesses.
By  solving the pending issues for the rationing losses, thus eliminating the Annex 5 controversy the MAE should function normally, allowing us to operate Eletrobolt and settle against the pool.
Total amounts for the sector represent about R$ 10 billion or US$3.8 billion at the current rates.
Our team has led the sector negotiations for months since the rationing, and have been instrumental in convincing the government of the need for implementing these changes.

Confidential - Attorney Client Privilege  

Please give me your thoughts on the attached proposal to resolve the "dangling chads" with AEP.

I have attached the proposal and a "value analysis" of the proposal, both of which I propose to send to AEP after we finalize our internal review and strategy. Based on my analysis of our contractual obligations, regulatory exposure, and potential litigation risks, I believe this settlement approach offers significant strategic advantages for Enron.

The key benefits of the proposal from Enron's perspective are the following:  

1. Removes us from the vagueness and uncapped exposure of the Ducote deal with Entex for additional costs.
Under the current arrangement, we face potential unlimited liability for cost overruns and project delays that are largely outside our control. The Ducote facility expansion has already exceeded initial projections by 23%, and engineering reports suggest further complications with environmental permitting that could add another $3-5 million in unexpected costs. Our legal team has reviewed the contract language and confirms that the "additional costs" provision is poorly defined and could expose us to claims for consequential damages. AEP can capture the economics of future gas deliveries to Entex associated with this capital expenditure, as they have the existing infrastructure and customer relationships to maximize returns on this investment.

2. Captures the leverage that AEP will have in the Entex audit.
AEP's operational control of the pipeline system gives them superior access to data, personnel, and documentation that will be critical in the ongoing regulatory audit. They have established relationships with the auditors and better institutional knowledge of historical operations. I think for ENA to pursue Entex independently would be difficult/time consuming and may lead to a tortious interference suit from AEP, particularly given their existing contractual relationship with Entex and their position as the primary operator. Our outside counsel has indicated that AEP could claim we are improperly interfering with their business relationships, which could result in additional litigation costs of $500K-$1M even if we ultimately prevail.

3. Gives up the interest payment we think AEP owes us.
Based on our contract analysis and the accounting records from Q2-Q4 of last year, we calculate AEP owes approximately $847,000 in interest payments on delayed settlements. This is true value we are giving up, but the legal costs to pursue this claim could easily reach $200-300K, and do we really want to fight with AEP in court over this (to the extent they are not bluffing about their counterclaims)? AEP has indicated they will dispute the calculation methodology and claim offsets for operational costs they absorbed during the transition period.

4. Removes us from having to process imbalances - saving manpower costs and further removing us from hassles with AEP.
Our operations team currently dedicates approximately 15-20 hours per week to processing these imbalances, which translates to roughly $75,000 annually in direct labor costs, plus additional overhead for systems maintenance and dispute resolution. AEP is better able to capture value from these imbalances than we are, since they have the pipe and can optimize flows in real-time. They also have existing automated systems that can handle the volume more efficiently, whereas we would need to invest an estimated $150,000 in system upgrades to properly manage the increasing transaction volume.

5. Gets us out of the Coastline lawsuit.
After reviewing the case files and settlement discussions, I'm pretty sure Coastline is at least owed the $1.4MM that we would contribute under this proposal. Our litigation counsel has advised that Coastline has a strong case on the contract interpretation issues, and proceeding to trial could result in a judgment significantly higher than the settlement amount. AEP has a chance to minimize any further costs through their operational expertise and existing vendor relationships, with total exposure capped by the value of the claim at a further $2.2MM. This removes our risk of additional liability if Coastline's damages claims prove to be higher than currently estimated.

Additionally, this settlement eliminates several other risk factors: (a) it resolves potential regulatory issues with FERC regarding our asset classification that could impact other transactions; (b) it allows us to redeploy the management time currently spent on these disputes to higher-value opportunities; and (c) it removes a contingent liability from our books that has been creating uncertainty in our quarterly reporting.

Please do not circulate this outside of the immediate legal team until we have completed our due diligence on the regulatory approval requirements.

Thanks,

Paul: Got your voice mail regarding Anthony Pescetti running for a FERC seat. Here are some quick thoughts that may help, and Sue likely has additional insights as well—I’d be happy to discuss further.

To start, Pescetti is a Republican assemblymember from the Sacramento area and previously served on the Sacramento Municipal Utility District board before joining the legislature. He became the Republican (minority) head of the assembly electricity oversight committee chaired by Rod Wright.

In the middle of his legislative career, Pescetti consistently favored utility interests. I don’t recall him ever opposing a pro-utility bill—in fact, just this past session, he sponsored legislation that would have cemented utility control over major parts of the gas industry and specifically would have locked out competition. That bill was strongly opposed by industry and ultimately defeated.

In the end, when it really mattered, Pescetti always sided with the utilities. Even when Assembly Republicans were doing a good job of bottling up Davis’ questionable bailout bills in Rod Wright’s committee, Pescetti seemed to go along, but more to tweak the Democrats than to foster competition. Importantly, he wasn’t a leader in these efforts—other, more junior committee members took the lead while Pescetti followed.

This is just a short update on the conference call just completed with  Michael Adewumi of Penn State, concerning the PCB pipeline modeling project  proposed for the Transwestern mainline system.
David Roensch, Dr. Adewumi  and myself discussed the latest proposal submitted by Adewumi and based upon  his answers to the technical and operational questions, it appears that the  model will yeild some useful information.
Adewumi was asked about the  simultaneous modeling of PCB's and arsenic and feels that the model can  address this situation.
He felt that by initiating the model to the pipeline  segement  selected for the study (between C/S 4 and C/S3) this information  could be projected to the other pipeline segments with physical and  elevational conditions not represented in the segment selected.
As is the  case with most projects of this nature, answers to some questions cannot be  addressed until we begin the process.
It appears that the next step in this process is to have Mike Terraso contact  Michael Adewumi.
David Roensch and I will be available to feed technical and  operational information to Adewumi for his modeling input.
It may also be in  the best interest of this project  to see a team of technical and operational  experts from Enron and Transwestern begin a  brain stroming of this project  during the data input stage to address issues related to the field cleaning  trials, both of the pipeline system and the C/S piping.
By working through  the process, we may be able to alleviate some potential concerns  and  increase the cleaning success.
Although Transwestern has been involved in  this type of cleaning for a number of years, based upon the liquids data  results, the system has met with variable success.
The more technical and  operational information we can incorporate into the model, the better will be  the modeling conclusions and results of the  cleaning activity.
