Subject: Clarification on Credit Derivatives Contract Structure and Appropriate Documentation

Dear [Recipient Name],

I am writing to discuss the structuring of credit derivatives contracts and to clarify whether these instruments should fall under the ISDA Master Agreement or the General Terms and Conditions (GTC).

Credit derivatives, such as credit default swaps (CDS), total return swaps, and credit-linked notes, typically involve the transfer of credit risk between parties. Given the complexity and standardized nature of these products, the industry standard is to document them under the ISDA Master Agreement framework. The ISDA Master Agreement, along with its credit derivatives definitions and confirmation templates, offers comprehensive coverage in terms of event definitions, settlement mechanics, and counterparty risk mitigants, which are critical for these types of contracts.

In contrast, the GTC is generally more suitable for straightforward cash or securities transactions and lacks the necessary provisions for managing the unique risks and contingencies inherent in credit derivatives. Relying solely on GTC for such contracts could result in inadequate legal protection and operational uncertainty.

Therefore, it is strongly recommended that credit derivatives contracts be documented under the ISDA Master Agreement structure to ensure consistency with market practice and to provide robust legal certainty for all parties involved.

Please let me know if you would like to discuss this in more detail.

Best regards,  
[Your Name]

Mark's first thought was that they would always go under a GTC, but  after reflection, perhaps we might want them to go under the master.
We need  to get this resolved because there is no global contract assigned to any of  the credit derivatives online, which is causing much trouble between Global  Contract and the online crew.

Subject: PRC Derivatives Transaction and Sovereign Immunity Risks

Dear [Recipient Name],

I hope this message finds you well.

I am writing to highlight certain considerations regarding derivatives transactions involving counterparties in the People’s Republic of China (PRC), specifically relating to sovereign immunity risks.

When transacting with PRC state-owned entities (including banks and corporations), parties should be aware that these entities may assert sovereign immunity in the event of legal proceedings, both domestically and abroad. While PRC law does permit state-owned enterprises to enter into commercial contracts and, in many cases, courts may find a waiver of immunity implied by commercial activity, the risk of a successful immunity claim cannot be fully eliminated without an express and enforceable waiver of sovereign immunity within transaction documentation.

Additionally, enforcement of foreign judgments or arbitral awards against PRC entities can be particularly challenging. Local courts may refuse enforcement if it is deemed to conflict with public interests or PRC sovereignty. Consequently, close attention should be paid to dispute resolution and enforceability provisions in ISDA Master Agreements or other derivatives documentation.

We recommend including explicit waiver of sovereign immunity language and assessing the counterparty’s asset location for enforceability purposes before entering into such transactions.

Please let us know if you need further information or wish to discuss this matter in greater detail.

Best regards,  
[Your Name]  
[Your Position]  
[Your Company]

Dear Western Region: The faint hum of the trading floor provided a backdrop as I would like to thank Phillip Allen for his leadership of the west desk for 2000 and 2001.
He will continue as Managing Director at Enron North America and trade a financial book for the natural gas trading group.
Phillip will be sitting near the western region, amidst the constant click of keyboards, and will continue to participate in our goal to analyze the western market fundamentals to maximize wholesale trading efforts.
I will be assuming all management responsibilities of the west trading group effective immediately.
I would like to take the opportunity to discuss our new organization for the Western Region trading group. A fresh, almost crisp scent of new beginnings seemed to fill the air.
I have organized a vertical based trading structure that clearly defines each employee's responsibilities going forward, a clear, sharp blueprint.
Our goal is to organize all of our efforts in the west such that we will offer Enron North America the most profitable wholesale trading model, a vision we can almost touch.
The most significant change to the western region organization will be Keith Holst's role as Director of West Fundamentals.
Keith will manage this unit from the west desk, bathed in the soft glow of monitors, while using the services of Enron's centralized fundamentals group, headed by Chris Gaskill.
Our western region Fundamentals group will be responsible for delivering the most complete and market sensitive data to the trading desk. This data, tangible and solid, will be our foundation.
We will all share in Keith's efforts to make our fundamental analysis the standard for all trading units within the company, creating a resonant ripple of insight.
West Origination, led by Barry Tycholiz, will play a larger role in our term trading efforts going forward.
They will be joining our desk for fundamental forecasting meetings and discussions, where the rustle of charts will guide our decisions.
Our goal is to capture a majority of the term risk management efforts of our customer base. The strong, steady pulse of our market engagement will grow.
We must succeed in capturing a majority of our customers' business to increase our share of lower risk earnings.
This contribution, along with our wholesale trading, will help our desk beat earnings expectations consistently, letting us taste the sweet success.
The West trading organization is structured to maximize profitability by sub-region.
The emphasis for the trading group will be to increase profitability and market information from each trader's sub-region.
We will be evaluated on how we organize and build the business and profitability in our respective trading areas. The smooth, well-oiled machinery of our operations will be evident.
This structure, however, does not preclude west traders from trading positions throughout the Western region and the North American gas market.
The West trading organization will be successful by creating accountability for trading responsibilities.
Please review the attached outline for the new trading structure, its lines clear and defined.
We will be meeting as a group to discuss the changes soon. The quiet anticipation is palpable.
The implementation of this structure will rely on our back office to set up the new books for each trader, a task requiring a firm and precise touch.
Sincerely,

From the Birmingham Sunday Mercury (7th Jan 2001)   Worker dead at desk for 5 days    Bosses of a publishing  firm are trying to work out why no one   noticed that one of their employees had been sitting dead at   his desk for FIVE DAYS before anyone asked if he was feeling   okay.
George Turklebaum, 51, who had been employed as a   proof-reader at a New York firm for 30 years, had a heart attack   in the open-plan office he shared with 23 other workers.
He   quietly passed away on Monday, but nobody noticed until   Saturday morning when an office cleaner  asked why he was   still working during the weekend.
His boss Elliot Wachiaski   said "George was always the first guy in each morning and the   last to leave at night, so no one found it unusual that he was in   the same position all that time and didn't say anything.
He was   always absorbed in his work and kept much to himself.
"A post   mortem examination revealed that he had been dead for five   days after suffering a coronary.
Ironically, George was   proofreading manuscripts of medical textbooks when he died.
You may want to give your co-workers a nudge or kick   occasionally.

4) When will the plan reach bankruptcy court?

Subject: Suggestions and Requests for Improving the Eterra Trading System

Hi Team,

Following my detailed workflow review with Sasha, I wanted to share several suggestions and requests to enhance the Eterra trading system:

1. **Streamline Order Entry Process:** We noticed extra steps in placing and modifying orders. Simplifying the interface and allowing for quick order amendments (e.g., drag-and-drop or in-line editing) would improve efficiency.
2. **Improved Real-time Notifications:** Currently, order status and execution notifications occasionally lag or lack detail. Introducing configurable, real-time alerts with detailed messages (including partial fills, cancellations, etc.) would help users stay better informed.
3. **Flexible Reporting and Export Options:** The ability to customize and export trading reports (e.g., by strategy, instrument, or time period) would allow for more effective analysis. Supporting additional formats such as XLSX and CSV is also recommended.
4. **Advanced Risk Management Tools:** Adding real-time risk dashboards and customizable alerts for position limits, exposure, and drawdowns would enhance control and transparency.
5. **Enhanced Audit Trails:** Providing more granular logs of user actions (such as modifications, cancellations, and bulk actions) with timestamps would support compliance requirements.
6. **API Documentation and Sandbox Access:** Improving the clarity of API documentation and setting up a sandbox environment would encourage smoother integration for external developers.

Please let us know which items are feasible in the short term and if further clarification is needed on any point.

Best regards,  
[Your Name]

John,  I met with Sasha today for approx.
3 hours.
We reviewed the exact process for inputting data into Eterra and verifying the trades prior to being sent to the QSE MOS.
Here are some suggestions that I made to Sasha for improving Eterra (the top of the list is the highest priority):   - Allow the Deal Entry screen to accept single entry trades, such as a simultaneous Buy from Calpine (South Zone) and a Sell to FPL (North Zone).
Currently, this has to be done by entering two trades, a purchase from Calpine (South Zone) to the Hourly Ercot book and a second entry of Hourly Ercot book     to FPL (North Zone).
Sasha said he is working on this, but problems are occurring due to the transmission between South and North.
- Change the process of increasing the Frontera generation.
The current process is to input a buy from Frontera into the Frontera book.
This is not very intuitive and we are still trying to work out an easier process.
(Possibly even having a button that we can click to indicate that    it is a purchase from Frontera.
Essentially, this would increase the EPMI mw's in the Ercot Portal.)
- Change the short name in <internal counterpary> & <external counterparty> to the actual long name, (i.e.
- elpasomeren to El Paso Merchant Energy)   - Give us a list of Counterparties and the appropriate QSE, (i.e.
- El Paso Merchant is actually APX)     So that we know what it will affect in the Ercot Portal.
- Match flow date to automatically update the Contract date.
One less step that we need to worry about.
I tried to impress upon Sasha that in trading "time is of the essence" and that we don't have much time to input data.
Therefore, we need to streamline the deal entry process and to make it more user friendly.
I realize that the first two items will take some time, but the last 3 items should be quick fixes.
I hope this helps.
Joe Capasso

To the attention of: Dr  Kenneth L. Lay Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Enron   Dear Dr Lay,  2001 was an extraordinary year!
As it draws to a close, I would like to share some of my thoughts with you.
First of all, I wanted to thank our members and constituents for their active engagement during the last 12 months, which helped us to move forward in our efforts to serve as a framework and catalyst for business and society to improve the state of the world.
In 2001 we implemented "Forum Plus" strategy, designed to advance critical issues on the global agenda through the creation of task forces and initiatives that integrate business, governments, international organizations, civil society, academics and technical experts.
Today, 11 task forces are already in place.
To provide an intellectual and strategic base for these activities, we have developed and computerized - with the help of our members and constituents - a comprehensive system for monitoring some 200 specific items on the global agenda.
This tracking process provides a foundation for action on these ongoing challenges.
To make our foundation a true multi-stakeholder platform we have created a number of consultative councils (e.g.
with NGOs, world religious leaders, academies of science, etc.)
and have, at the same time, strengthened the role of the business community inside our organization.
It is worth noting that despite the negative trends in the global economy, 2001 was a successful year for all of our activities.
This shows that even in difficult times there is a great demand for increased interaction among global decision-makers, and for top-level community building.
The most difficult decision the Forum had to take this year was to move our Annual Meeting from Davos to New York in the aftermath of the tragic events of 11 September.
From 31 January to 4 February 2002, leaders from business, governments, academia, religions, the media and civil society will have a first opportunity to develop an integrated response to these new circumstances.
The Annual Meeting 2002 is organized around six major challenges we are facing as a global community:  1.
Restoring Sustained Growth 2.
Achieving Security, Addressing Vulnerabilities 3.
Redefining Business Challenges 4.
Reducing Poverty and Achieving Equity 5.
Sharing Values and Respecting Differences 6.
Re-evaluating Leadership and Governance  The Annual Meeting in New York will be characterized by a workshop-style approach where all participants will have an opportunity to engage in shared learning and to have a collective impact.
The programme is designed to stimulate discussion and provide insights that will help us better cope with the fragility of our times.
The response to our invitations has been overwhelming: All the key personalities will be present.
Please note that this year, instead of sending Christmas cards, we have made a donation to the Nelson Mandela Foundation to help build schools for needy children.
My 150 colleagues and I look forward to joining forces with you in the New Year, in the spirit of entrepreneurship in the global public interest, to "improve the state of the world."
My very best wishes accompany you in your contemplation at the end of the year and particularly for a healthy and successful 2002.
Klaus Schwab Founder and President World Economic Forum

Hey everyone, Just finished working my first full week at Deer Valley.
The resort opened friday and from tues through sunday I worked with the other bakers to get items prepped and inventories stocked up for the mad rush of skiers expected over the weekend.
I am enjoying working under the pastry chef at the lodge I am at.
He is very dilligent about coming over and making sure you understand the how's and why's of the recipe you are making.
His explanations are scientific when they need to be and straightforward when they don't need to be long and drawn out.
I'm confident that I will learn a lot from the other chefs and bakers there as well.
The first few days were very frustrating.
There are a group of bakers, level 3's, who work at the lodge every winter and supervise the new bakers.
There were a few tasks that I was assigned to do along w/ these level 3 bakers.
We were cutting cakes in half and I was doing it the way Patrick always showed me and she said that I shouldn't do it that way ...to do it another way.
Then one of the girls at my level with the $40k diploma from the CIA asked me if I had ever cut a cake before (like asking someone if they are retarded).
I couldn't see straight I was so frustrated.
Later, I was shaping baguettes..again..the way I learned...and the level 3 told me to do it another way...and that our boss Steve who studied bread could show me later since he knows so much.
Well when he came over later ...he did it almost exactly the same way I did.
There are lots of stories like this from those first few days.
I had to bite my tongue a lot.
One girl claims she can tell when bread is done proofing by looking at it...and doesn't have to touch it (why wouldn't you touch it..thats the best part).
I might believe that from someone in their 40's but not a 20 something who has only been baking a few years.
So I went home completely frustrated the first 3 days, but I had to remind myself that school was 2yrs ago for me and for many of these girls school was last month or a few months ago.
We have a lot of people in the kitchen who hail from the CIA, which for those of you who might not know..it is a school that cranks out culinary grads for around $40,000 for the entire program.

Tracy called me at work.  
A water pipe broke under the street between her house and the old Hamilton house.  
She said water was shooting everywhere and that they were to turn off the water for at least 5 hours.  

Well, as I was leaving work, I could picture the scene: the early afternoon sun glinting off gushing water as kids tiptoed nearby on their bikes, watching the commotion. The city crew rushed in, orange cones popping up like mushrooms, and an old neighbor, Mr. Tibbets, stood at the corner shaking his head as he sipped coffee from his green thermos.  

They worked fast because when I got home at 6:00, I had water.  
So I made some turkey soup. The smell drifted through the house, and for a moment, even the chaos outside faded as I diced carrots and listened to the quiet gurgle of a fixed water line.  

But Willow Lane will be torn up for a while as it just buckled the cement.  
The hole was about 7 feet down according to Tracy.  

Good thing this didn't happen on Thanksgiving!  
I have a foundation man coming out next week to check the foundation.  

Tracy seems to have a similar problem. Maybe we can get a two for one deal.  

John, I need your book list at Amazon.com this week. No excuses!  
Oh, tell Jeannie that I finished her soup this evening for dinner. She's a good cook!  

Have a good week guys.  
Love, Mom

Given the growth in EES it has become apparent that it is time to consolidate the risk functions between EES and EWS.
This will provide EES with the systems, resources and risk expertise of the wholesale energy groups necessary for it to continue to grow and take advantage of current market opportunities.
With this in mind and in agreement with the management of EES, two new risk groups inside Enron Americas will be formed to provide EES with pricing, structuring, retail and wholesale commodity risk management, logistics and back-office services.

We have asked Rogers Herndon, currently Vice President-Trading in the Eastern Power Group to manage this function in the Eastern Interconnect (this includes both gas and power).
Rogers will continue to report to Kevin Presto.
We have asked Don Black, formerly Vice President-EES Risk Management and Sourcing, to manage this function in the Western U.S.  Don will manage this group from Houston and will report to Tim Belden.
These groups will work very closely with EES to pursue shared goals while ensuring close coordination with the wholesale gas and power trading organizations.
These changes are effective immediately.
Please congratulate Rogers and Don on their new roles.
John Lavorato & Louise Kitchen

The news, bizarre as it sounds, arrived moments ago via a frantic call from our insider: they are calling the Assembly members back.
So it appears that the Assembly leadership will at least make a run at this.
Our phones are ringing off the hook as new details trickle in, and across the city, industry leaders are already scrambling, pulling people into urgent strategy sessions.
Some key considerations: From the top floors of the Capitol, the Governor's office is applying immense, visible pressure – veiled threats and stern public statements – on the Legislature to finally deliver something.
You can feel the palpable fear among legislators of being singled out, of facing the Governor's wrath and public scorn for having "done nothing."
Because the Assembly's chambers have been largely quiet, with no substantive movement on major bills, the only item now seemingly viable on their docket is 78.
The Assembly could not agree to the Speaker's bill because it felt the bill was too far to the left; but 78 is even more one-sided.
So there's a reasonable likelihood that 78 would have to be amended considerably in order to get the support necessary to get voted out.
Once voted out of the Assembly, it would have to go back to the Senate, where the Senate would have to approve it.
Again, the Senate desks are currently empty, the chambers dark, having officially adjourned. This means Burton would have to issue an urgent recall, chasing down senators scattered across their districts, a task made harder by the stony silence from his own office – there's no indication at this time that Burton is inclined to even return, let alone reconvene.
Moreover, Burton has publicly, defiantly stated his position: he's not interested in making any changes to 78, that "it's 78 or nothing."
Consequently, for the Senate (i.e., Burton) to vote it out, it would first have to agree to the Assembly's amendments.
The chasm between the Assembly and the Senate on these issues has been wide and unyielding, marked by weeks of stalled negotiations and public disagreements.
All that said, this Legislature operates on its own peculiar, often unpredictable logic, a place where sudden reversals are not uncommon, and absolutely nothing can be counted out.
We are therefore lighting the late-night lamps in our war room, operating under the assumption that even with these odds, 78 could still somehow move forward.
Will report back as information becomes available.
Best,

Dear Team,

This email provides an update following the recent hearing.

The court addressed our Document Preservation Motion. After deliberation, the judge granted the motion, emphasizing the critical importance of ensuring all relevant materials are protected and available for discovery. We will be circulating the specific terms and obligations outlined in the order shortly, and it is imperative that all parties comply fully and immediately.

Regarding the matter of Lead Counsel, the court has officially confirmed [Name of Lead Counsel] will serve in this capacity, effective immediately. This decision provides clear direction for our litigation strategy moving forward. [Name of Lead Counsel] will be reaching out to the core legal team to delineate roles and responsibilities and to coordinate the next steps in our approach.

[Your Name/Legal Department]
source_text:
The court held a hearing today on the motion by some of the plaintiffs for an order regarding the preservation of documents.
The motions were directed primarily to Arthur Andersen and, to a lesser degree, to Enron.
None of your names were mentioned at the hearing.
Arthur Andersen and one of the plaintiffs' lawyers had agreed on a proposed order for preserving documents.
Other plaintiffs' lawyers said that the agreed order was not stringent enough.
With respect to Enron, there is some doubt as to whether the court can enter any order regarding Enron, because that may be the exclusive purview of the bankruptcy court.
Although the issue of which attorney should be appointed lead counsel was not technically before the court, most of the hearing was consumed with the various plaintiffs' lawyers arguing that the court should select them to be lead counsel.
The court said that it would not rule on the motion regarding preservation of documents until after 3:00 tomorrow.
All of the plaintiffs' lawyers are to get together in the next 24 hours to see if they can agree amongst themselves as to what they want the court to do.
The court said she would also consider whether Arthur Andersen was willing to agree to whatever order plaintiffs' all might agree upon.
The judge suggested that she would be selecting the lead plaintiff (and counsel) within the next few weeks.

Dear Team,

I am writing to inform you of upcoming leadership changes and management restructuring at Enron. As part of our ongoing efforts to strengthen our company and position ourselves for future success, the Board of Directors has approved a realignment of key management roles and the introduction of new leadership within several divisions.

Effective immediately, several senior executives will be transitioning into new roles, while others will be joining the organization to bring fresh perspectives and expertise to our operations. These changes are intended to enhance operational efficiency, improve oversight, and better align our leadership structure with Enron’s strategic objectives.

We are confident that these moves will allow us to respond more quickly to market demands and continue delivering value to our clients, employees, and shareholders. Over the coming weeks, further details will be provided regarding specific leadership appointments and departmental restructuring. We encourage everyone to support one another during this time of transition.

If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to your manager or HR representative.

Thank you for your continued dedication and commitment to Enron’s success.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]  
[Your Position]

Jeff,  Please accept my apologies for the slight delay in getting back to you on the message board regarding this week's API forecast.
I'd like to take a minute of your time to highlight what we are doing to address all our concerns over our forecasts and how we are actively seeking to produce better results that we are all comfortable with and that provide useful insight and tradable information to our colleagues on the trading desks.
As I am sure you know, forecasting the API's is not as scientific as other industry data such as the AGA's.
The API is not consistently clear as to how it measures crude demand and this week's data is  a clear example of this in that there is a discrepancy of 1.2 million b/d between crude runs and the demand figure shown by the API.
Each week the basis of measuring crude demand changes slightly.
To address this we are looking at finding ways of predicting what we call the API Curve Ball Factor through a  variety of regressions / moving averages analysis.
The second area we are in the process of perfecting is imports data.
We are working closely with IT and Net Works to scrape real time shipping information in order to give us a better handle on crude coming in to the country.
We are also recruiting a Quants PhD from Vince Kaminski's group who will be able to bring a slightly more scientific skill set to our team of business / economics skill sets.
Please be assured that this issue is one we are giving the utmost priority to addressing.
Having only recently taken on responsibility for the crude and products fundamentals team I have not had much opportunity to discuss issues with you.
Please be assured that I am available at any time to discuss this, or any other, issue with you.
Best regards,

In Washington, the stakes for the coming year could not be higher. The decisions Congress makes on comprehensive energy and electricity legislation will directly impact American families, businesses, and our economic recovery. We’ll be digging into whether lawmakers will take bold action—or let critical opportunities slip away—while millions watch and hope for change.

Our team will closely track the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s aggressive push for regional transmission organizations and wholesale competition. The outcomes here could shape not only the reliability of our power grids, but the lives of consumers across the country, determining whether electricity stays affordable and accessible as demand hits new highs.

As 2002 dawns, we know so many are worried about what the future holds. On Wednesday, former Assistant Secretary of Energy Robert Gee will be in our Washington bureau to break down the fragile U.S. relationship with OPEC, a partnership that has left our country vulnerable to price shocks and uncertainty. He'll also offer an honest assessment of whether Texas’s move to retail competition will empower consumers—or expose them to new risks.

We're paying especially close attention to what’s happening in Houston as Texas plunges into electricity deregulation on January 1. Our Houston bureau’s early reports suggest both hope and anxiety, with families and businesses bracing to see whether the promised benefits of choice actually materialize or if unforeseen problems threaten their security and pocketbooks just as winter bills hit home.

John S. Herold, Inc. CEO Arthur Smith will also join us—his latest research points to the very real possibility of earnings shockwaves ahead. Dear Market Participant,  In the interest of not flooding the webmaster with constant changes (new PTIDs or new participant names) to the UCAP forms (Certification, Bid Forms, and Offer Forms), I will be updating the forms about once per month.
Since you will need a methodology to work around missing information, the new forms have codes that will allow you to enter undefined PTIDs and undefined new participants.
PTID number 999999 is used for a resource that has not been assigned a number.
NewLSE is used for a new Load Serving Entity that has not been assigned a "Registrant Name" NewSuppl is used for a new Supplier that has not been assigned a "Registrant Name"  NOTE that if you use any of the above, you must describe your intentions in the comments cell of the form being submitted.
Other Changes  ISOSu is the prefix for sales or purchases that occurred as a result of NYISO transactions during the supplemental process.
The supplemental process is implemented when there is insufficient UCAP available within a location and the NYISO must purchase UCAP from outside the location where the shortage has occurred to meet the NYCA reliability requirements.
PTID numbers to be used when identifying UCAP purchased through the NYISO auction have been assigned.
The PTID numbers range from 1 to 38 and are related to auctions or the supplemental processes.
For example, a participant who is selling UCAP that was previously purchased in the summer strip auction would enter PTID number 1 on the Offer form when selling into a subsequent ISO auction.
A list of PTID numbers is now available on the instruction page of the auction Offer forms.
Reminder  When identifying an ISO auction, please remember that you must think in terms of the procurement period for the first auction month when the transaction took place.
For example, on May 15 (the auction for the upcoming months of June through October) 3MW were transacted for the months of June and August.
The auction reference that you will use for both the June and August transactions are ISOMoJun.
The same auction reference would be used if on May 15, the transactions were for August and September.
When completing the Certification Form, do not net transactions.
Lets say that you are awarded 25 MW from the Strip Auction and later move (purchase or sell) 5 MW through a bilateral.
Your entries on the form would show the 25 MW strip auction transaction on one line and your second line would show the 5 MW bilateral transaction.
You can not use a value of 20MW on one line.
Each and Every Month you must submit your certification form.
Regards,

Greetings, my name is Tori Kuykendall (One Pass BJ927934).
My husband, Patrick (One Pass VF751282), and I have held One Pass memberships for several years, and we have also achieved elite status multiple times.
Additionally, we exclusively utilize the Chase Continental Visa, and my husband holds a President's Club membership.
Continental has been my preferred airline for as long as I've been making my own travel bookings, and I've consistently been a highly content customer.
However, I encountered a very negative experience this morning.
I made a vacation booking on September 4th for a trip from Houston to New York set for December 1st.
Subsequent to making that reservation, I became pregnant, and my doctor informed me last week that I would be unable to travel on December 1st because of pregnancy-related complications.
My physician informed me that I might be entirely unable to fly throughout my pregnancy, which is expected to conclude in June.
This morning, I discussed the circumstances with Leroy Peterson, who stated that his only option was to provide me with a credit expiring on September 5th, 2001, and that a $75 service fee would be applied the next time I reserve a ticket for myself or my husband.
I realize that this aligns with the standard policy applied if I had simply changed my mind about taking a vacation this weekend.
From my perspective, this policy is unacceptable when medical complications arise.
Given my circumstances, it is improbable that my husband and I will be able to arrange a vacation by September 2001, especially since we anticipate having a two-month-old infant by then.
I repeatedly inquired with Leroy if there was another individual who could assist me or whom I could speak with to obtain an exemption from your policy.
I mentioned that I was able to furnish a medical certificate if required.
His response was quite impolite; he declared, "There's no need to ask me the same question seven different times – I've already informed you NO!"
Approximately a month ago, I had to cancel a business flight with Southwest Airlines for the identical reason, though I had hoped to be fit to fly again by this point.
To provide some context, your rival airline was exceedingly cooperative.
They acknowledged my medical documentation, issued a credit valid for a year, and will permit me to transfer the ticket to another individual if I remain unable to utilize it myself.
That particular ticket was also purchased as a non-reimbursable fare.
Despite consistently choosing Continental for my personal journeys, the way I have been handled during this challenging period has certainly caused me to reconsider my future travel selections.
Should you be able to provide any assistance, I would be extremely grateful.

Tanya: I just received a revised draft of the ISDA Schedule for the XYZ Corporation master agreement.

There is just 1 point that I want to raise with you.

You may recall that in Credit Event Upon Merger we created a special exception for XYZ Corporation in connection with their upcoming corporate reorganization which stated that either the transferee or its Credit Support Provider would have to have a Credit Rating of BBB- or better from S&P OR Baa3 or better from Moody's.

They now have added this same concept as a carve-out/exception to the "transfer" provisions in section 7(a) of the ISDA Master Agreement, such that upon any transfer of the agreement, the other party (our bank) cannot withhold its consent to such transfer if the transferee provides a Guaranty from an entity that meets the above ratings test (BBB-/Baa3 minimum rating requirement).

Are you okay with this as a general carve-out for all types of transfers under section 7?

Our typical language is that we can withhold our consent to any transfer unless the transferee provides a guaranty that is satisfactory to us in our sole discretion.

Carol

There seems to be some confusion around which DPR captures the credit reserve and consumption premium reserves, and which balance sheet these items fall on. Based on my discussions with both Don and Kevin, my understanding is that, going forward, since EES is being granted origination (which would be the residual after all reserves are applied), all prudency/reserve items will rest on the WhEES DPR. As a result, the EES DPR will display only a single net origination line item.

However, we do need to capture the activity related to DSM in the EES DPR (including some portion of credit reserve and drift). Until we have the system capability to track this activity separately, it may need to remain lumped into the broader WhEES category.

This approach aligns with the idea that all future exposures—whether from wholesale price movement, tariff changes, credit exposure, or other risks—should be borne by EWS. Therefore, they will require the appropriate reserves to offset any realized activity. Importantly, the balance sheet reserves associated with these items are already recorded in the ledgers rolling up under EWS. Reflecting these positions on the WhEES DPR would ensure consistency with our current accounting practices.

If anyone disagrees with this proposed treatment, please respond to all parties above so we can resolve any outstanding issues. In the absence of objections, I recommend moving the credit reserve over at the next possible opportunity.

P.S. This approach reflects our current operating assumptions. If there are future changes in the allocation between EWS and EES (for example, regarding accounts receivable), we may need to revisit the treatment of the credit reserve.

Distributed Power: A Forthcoming Major Investment Opportunity?

Given that current electricity demand is expanding beyond the capacity of available supply, and nationwide electric deregulation initiatives have yielded inconsistent outcomes, distributed power may well represent a significant emerging trend, as noted by Bear Stearns analyst Robert Winters. With the rapid proliferation of technology-intensive, electricity-dependent companies, and the increasing frequency of blackouts and brownouts due to declining reliability of large power grids, the analyst highlights distributed energy services as a potential remedy, and perhaps "a prominent investment opportunity for the forthcoming decade."

In Winters' 250-page report, "Distributed Energy Services-The World's Power and Transportation Industries: Set for a Revolution-Part 2," he scrutinizes technologies and companies within the distributed energy services sector that are positioned to capitalize on the prevailing circumstances. "Owing to significant technological advancements and energy deregulation, a surge of novel investment in the power industry has commenced. We anticipate that this forthcoming era in the power industry could parallel the surge of investments that inundated the telecommunications industry subsequent to the dissolution of AT&T in the early 1980s," Winters stated. "Enterprises and municipalities must identify strategies to ensure the provision of high-quality, reliable power," Winters further remarked.

According to his research, microturbines are optimally positioned among the novel technologies capable of exerting an immediate impact on electric generation. He predicated his recommendation on the attributes of microturbines, specifically their compact size, low noise emission, efficiency, and high versatility. "They can be deployed as a primary power source, a supplementary power source, or as an an alternative in instances of significant fluctuations in traditional energy prices," the analyst articulated. "Microturbines can additionally be utilized in remote locales, including developing nations, which lack access to electrical grids." Another compelling characteristic of microturbines pertains to their fuel requirements. These units frequently utilize natural gas, but are also capable of employing several other fuel types.

Within the study, the analyst further examined fuel cells, flywheel technology, and established reciprocating engine technologies, such as diesel engines and Stirling engines, observing their current resurgence. Subsequent to the report, Winters commenced coverage on two distributed energy companies. He designated Active Power, a company pioneering flywheel technology, with a "buy" rating, and Capstone Turbine Corp., a leading manufacturer of microturbines, as "attractive." These companies are presented in addition to two fuel cell companies he currently monitors. Ballard Power currently carries a "buy" recommendation, while Plug Power is rated neutral.

Prescribing Ritalin: Who Decides—Doctors or Lawyers?

Monday, June 18, 2001, 9:30 a.m.–Noon Wohlstetter Conference Center, Twelfth Floor, AEI

The diagnosis and treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is one of the most urgent and contentious issues facing the medical community today. On one side, some physicians and psychologists caution that we are at risk of “medicalizing” childhood—turning normal developmental variation or challenging behaviors into conditions requiring medication. On the other, there are clinicians who prescribe stimulants such as Ritalin at the first sign of inattention or hyperactivity in a child.

While concerns about overdiagnosis deserve careful consideration, the overwhelming consensus among mental health professionals is clear: ADHD is a real, impairing condition, and stimulant therapies like Ritalin are proven, effective treatments for countless children who would otherwise struggle needlessly. The stakes for these children and their families are enormous; without proper intervention, ADHD can undermine academic success, relationships, and long-term well-being.

Yet into this medically grounded debate, a wave of litigation has introduced confusion and suspicion. Lawyers, representing a class of parents, have now filed lawsuits against both the maker of Ritalin and the American Psychiatric Association, alleging a conspiracy to “invent” ADHD for corporate gain. These lawsuits disregard the established scientific evidence and threaten to deny children access to treatments that could transform their lives.

This conference will provide a rigorous overview of the ADHD controversy—both the medical facts and the legal challenges now confronting clinicians and families. Experts will assess the reality of ADHD, the role of evidence-based therapy, and the broader consequences of allowing courtroom battles to drive medical decision-making for vulnerable children. Please join us for this important and timely discussion, followed by a question and answer period.

We plan to have three during the current academic year.
For those of you unfortunate enough to have missed the first Forum, the format works like this:  we'll have dinner, and then a panel of Harvard grads will give brief introductions to the evening's topic from their perspective, and then we will all engage the topic for ourselves in a moderated discussion.
The panel members will be knowledgeable, but not so expert that anyone will be intimidated.

You will come away knowing your fellow Club members better than ever - maybe better than you ever wanted.

Some will identify the critical factors in achieving success, while others will argue that all personal planning is an exercise in self-delusion.
We are confident that the discussion will be informative and lively.

I thought that this is something to think about as we contemplate war...
I have to admit that I am caught between the feelings of needing to act with violence to defend and needing to act with compassion to understand.
> What can you do TODAY...this very moment?
A central teaching in most spiritual traditions is: What you wish to experience, provide for another.
Look to see, now, what it is you wish to experience-in your own life, and in the world.
Then see if there is another for whom you may be the source of that.
If you wish to experience peace, provide peace for another.
If you wish to know that you are safe, cause another to know that they are safe.
If you wish to better understand seemingly incomprehensible things, help another to better understand.
If you wish to heal your own sadness or anger, seek to heal the sadness or anger of another.
Those others are waiting for you now.
They are looking to you for guidance, for help, for courage, for strength, for understanding, and for assurance at this hour.
Most of all, they are looking to you for love.

It's time to jump back into the lending game!  
Here's the situation: The STSW desk will be 20 MW short at peak (4C-345kv) per the El Paso lending agreement. The day-ahead sale price stands at $27.05. To manage this, please purchase the necessary volume under the STWHOURLY desk and execute an inter-desk sale to STSW, ensuring our positions are perfectly balanced.

Before you get started, a quick but crucial reminder: inter-desk swaps are NOT the same as annuities.  
- You cannot net the day's volume and swap out in just one hour.  
- To stay flat, you MUST buy and sell the same amount each hour throughout the day.

Since it's been a while, let’s walk through the process:  
1. After covering the STSW short in the real-time market, sell back to El Paso at $0 to stay net zero.  
2. Adjust the day-ahead purchase price from El Paso (account 794022) to $2 to account for the lending service fee.

If anything is unclear or you want to double-check your steps, don’t hesitate to reach out—questions are always welcome!

NRG Energy Inc. holds market-based rate authorization from FERC, which permits the company to engage in wholesale physical power trading activities across multiple regions. 5. **Credit Requirements**: Meet credit and collateral requirements established by ISOs/RTOs and counterparties

- Maintain adequate credit facilities for trading operations

Charlene,

As promised, I have outlined below the key points for your consideration ahead of our meeting on Wednesday morning. I’m not familiar with your agenda, so please review these at your discretion to determine which items may be appropriate to discuss.

Background:  
As a long-time advocate of the analyst program, I have grown increasingly concerned over the last several months as I’ve observed rising frustration among fellow program supporters—many of whom play integral roles in recruiting and providing analyst rotations. Their involvement has been instrumental in attracting strong candidates to the Merchant Services Analyst Program.

To coordinate and clarify our concerns, I initiated a meeting (announced at Rick Causey’s staff meeting) with a group of committed colleagues. Our goal was to articulate our feedback and discuss constructive ways to continue supporting and improving the program. The meeting took place on March 28 and included:

- Brenda Herod, ENA - Energy Operations Executive Lead - LSU  
- Brent Price, ENA - Energy Operations Executive Lead - UT  
- Jeff Sommers, CALME Executive Lead - University of Florida  
- Ed Coats, Corp. Tax, Core Team Member - UT, A&M, LSU, and University of Florida  
- Sally Beck, ENA - Energy Operations Executive Lead - UT and OU  
- Carolyn Barrett, EBS  
- Howard Selzer, Enron Global E&P  

Summary of Concerns and Discussion Points:  

1. **One Program or Two:**  
Before fall 1999 campus recruiting, it was announced there would be a single analyst program. However, little clarity followed regarding what this would mean in practice. In reality, the MSAP and Commercial Analyst programs continued to operate separately, especially in terms of recruiting, rotations, and orientation. This has left those of us leading recruitment efforts uncertain and less effective in representing the program on campus.

2. **Single Start Date:**  
The fixed analyst start date of July 17 is proving to be impractical and inflexible, especially for an innovative company. It does not accommodate December graduates or align well for undergraduates finishing in May.

3. **Lack of Communication:**  
Despite our deep commitment to the MSAP, we have received minimal updates or information about the program’s direction. We've heard rumors of "tracks," but lack concrete details. Some of us were aware of the single July start date, while others were not.

4. **Commercial Focus Too Heavy:**  
Current materials, staff interactions, and interview processes are heavily weighted towards commercial interests, with little understanding of support needs.

5. **Lack of Input from Key Supporters:**  
Given the significant time and effort many of us invest in MSAP, we are concerned that our input has not been actively sought in guiding the program's direction. For example, major decisions—such as the single start date—seem to have been made without valuable feedback from core supporters.

6. **Perceived Step Backward:**  
With a previously dedicated leadership team and staff, the MSAP made notable progress in campus consistency, candidate quality, acceptance rates, and participant pride. Over the last nine months, however, we have sensed a diminished focus on the program. We are eager to work with you to reinvigorate engagement and enthusiasm.

Thank you for your attention to these points. I look forward to our discussion and to working together for the continued success of the program.

From the 12/11/01 New Dem Daily.
Please let the Colorado DLC know what  you think.
This week the long, windy debate in Washington over a so-called economic  stimulus package will likely be resolved one way or another.
Putting aside  all the partisan finger-pointing as to who is responsible for this or that  twist or turn in the process, the bottom line is very clear: Republicans  are unwilling to support any stimulus package that does not include  significant new cuts in tax rates for wealthy individuals and  corporations.
We think that's too high a price to pay for the modest  relief efforts for the unemployed that should be the focus of this legislation.
The overall economy is not in as bad a shape as many feared at the  beginning of this debate.
Fiscal stimulus is already being supplied by new  federal spending related to the war on terrorism and homeland defense.
The  tax rate cuts Republicans demand will in any event have no positive  short-term impact on the economy, and could damage its long-range prospects  by boosting future federal budget deficits.
In effect, the GOP is holding  unemployment relief hostage to yet another installment in its relentless  drive for tax cuts targeted to high earners.
It's time for Democrats to call the whole thing off, and call the  Republicans' bluff on unemployment relief by decoupling it from tax rate  cuts.
Congress should be debating whether to cancel some of the high-end  tax cuts enacted earlier this year, in order to pay for the war on  terrorism.
Instead, Congressional Republicans have spent months talking  about new demands on public funds for the Americans who are least  vulnerable in the economic slowdown, and least likely to make personal  sacrifices in the war effort at home or abroad.
If fiscal discipline means anything at all, it means a willingness to  resist these sorts of demands.
New Democrats favor bipartisan compromises  in the pursuit of the national interest, but not in the pursuit of special  interests.
A deal with Republicans to secure new tax rate cuts would not  be a compromise between "Left" and "Right," but between right and wrong.

**BREAKTHROUGH IN FLANGE DESIGN: Revolutionary Workshop Unveils Game-Changing Industry Standards**

The engineering world is about to witness a seismic shift in bolted flange design. After decades of relying on traditional methods, groundbreaking tightness-based design rules are poised to transform how we approach gasket constants and flange engineering forever.

PVRC'S WORKSHOP ON TIGHTNESS-BASED BOLTED FLANGE GASKET CONSTANTS AND DESIGN RULES
February 6 & 7, 2002, Safety Harbor Florida

REGISTER NOW AND WATCH FOR FUTURE ANNOUNCEMENTS ON PVRC'S WEBSITE AT WWW.FORENGINEERS.ORG

Description
You must attend this workshop to help keep your job knowledge useful by understanding the new design rules for bolted flanged joints!
Are you ready for the New Tightness-Based Gasket constants and flange design changes that are about to replace the traditional constants and rules?
This workshop will get you ready with focus on three critical areas that apply to both ASME Section VIII flanges and standard B16 Joints.
The New Tightness-Based Rules Gasket Qualification and Selection Latest On Analysis and Assembly of Bolted Joints This Two-Day Workshop is a "must" for those needing advance information and know-how about applying the recently developed gasket constants and flange design rules.
The tightness-based rules accommodate levels of permissible joint leakage, representing a new basis for design criteria and opening additional choices and decisions for users and designers.
Attendees will gain detailed knowledge about several topics focussing on the new gasket constants and design rules and particularly on issues relating to leakage criteria and associated choices.
The tightness concept is also extended to elevated temperature gasket qualification and selection, and know-how for efficient joint assembly and making zero leakage plant operation a realistic goal is presented.
Several industry experts will lead workshop sessions including: Bob Mikitka, Jim Payne, Michel Derenne, Yves Birembaut, Ron winter, Jerry Waterland, Rod Mueller, Anita Bausman, Jim Frew Hildegarde Zeres, Warren Brown, Ed Hayman, Bill Koves, and David Reeves.
Attendees will receive a bound collection of the presentations and guidelines and recommendations.
For additional information contact Welding Research Council at 212-591-7956 or www.forengineers.org/pvrc

Good Morning Sara,

I'm writing to you regarding the CSFB 2001 Equity Swap Basket documentation. Following our last discussion, I've compiled a summary of key issues and additional recommendations:

1.  **Master ISDA Agreement with Credit Suisse First Boston (Europe) Limited:** The status remains under Credit Review.

2.  **Definitions:** Please ensure the following amendments are made:
    *   **a) Interest Payment Date:** Should state "3 business days after the Valuation Date."
    *   **b) Reference Price:** Amend the phrase "...last regular way trade..." to "...Official Closing Price..." in (i) and (ii)(b)(iii).
    *   **c) Securities:** Omit the reference to "Bonds." The definition should read: "are the securities specified as such in the Confirmation."
    *   **d) Valuation Date(s):** Confirm dates as: October 15, 2001, November 15, 2001, ... October 15, 2002.

3.  **Section 5.1 (i):** The reference to "Bonds" should be omitted. This section should be revised to read: "If a Security pays a dividend or makes another distribution, the payment to be made by the Seller shall be equal to the gross amount of the cash dividend or distribution per share (excluding for the avoidance of doubt any tax credits), as the case may be, multiplied by the Dividend Percentage, multiplied by the Contract Quantity."

    Additionally, we recommend including a definition for "Dividend Payment Date" as: "The Equity Payment Date relating to the Valuation Date(s) on which the relevant Dividend Period ends."

    And a "Dividend Amount" definition should be added, stating: "100% of all ordinary cash dividends where; (i) the ex-dividend date occurs during the period from the day following the Trade Date to and including the final Valuation Date and (ii) the date on which the related ordinary cash dividend would have been received by persons who held the Shares comprising the Basket during such period is during the relevant Dividend Period."

    Regarding **Section 5.2 "Potential Adjustment Event":** We strongly recommend replacing the current language with the Intra-Period Adjustment language utilized in the Enron Credit Confirmation. The existing section grants CSFB undue discretion to "determine" the provisions of Intra-Period Adjustments, including additional payments or adjustments to the Opening Price or Contract Quantity. This level of control for CSFB is unacceptable. The proposed Intra-Period Adjustment language is comprehensive and ensures fair, predefined provisions.

4.  **Schedule to Basket Swaps:**
    *   **a) Applicable Interest Rate Cycle:** Should read "1 month."
    *   **b) Termination Date:** Should read "1 year."
    *   **c) Business Day Convention:** Should be the standard ISDA "Modified Following Business Day Convention" language.

5.  **Annex Structure:** An Annex structure should be included to facilitate real-time monitoring of positions and any subsequent adjustments within the Equity Swap Basket throughout the deal term.

Please let me know if you would like to schedule a meeting to discuss this documentation in further detail.

Regards,

Subject: Guidelines for Electricity Cuts

Dear Residents,

This email outlines important guidelines regarding electricity cuts that may occur due to various reasons, including scheduled maintenance, unforeseen outages, or load management. Our aim is to ensure your safety and minimize inconvenience during these periods.

Please keep the following points in mind:

1.  **Preparation is Key:**
    *   **Charge Devices:** Ensure mobile phones, laptops, and power banks are fully charged, especially if an outage is anticipated.
    *   **Flashlights & Batteries:** Keep flashlights or battery-powered lanterns easily accessible and ensure you have fresh batteries. Avoid using candles unsupervised.
    *   **Water Supply:** If you rely on an electric pump for water, fill a bucket or two for basic needs.

2.  **Safety Precautions During an Outage:**
    *   **Unplug Appliances:** Disconnect sensitive electronics and major appliances (like TVs, computers, refrigerators) to protect them from power surges when electricity is restored.
    *   **Turn Off Lights:** Switch off most lights to prevent a sudden drain on the system and surprise when power returns. Leave one light on to signal when power is restored.
    *   **Food Safety:** Keep refrigerator and freezer doors closed as much as possible to maintain cold temperatures. Food typically remains safe for up to 4 hours in a refrigerator and 48 hours in a full freezer (24 hours if half full).
    *   **Generator Use:** If using a portable generator, always operate it outdoors in a well-ventilated area, far from windows and doors, to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

3.  **Communication and Reporting:**
    *   **Stay Informed:** We will endeavour to communicate planned outages in advance via [mention specific channels, e.g., community portal, email, notice boards]. For unplanned outages, we will provide updates as soon as information becomes available.
    *   **Reporting Outages:** If you experience an outage and have not received prior notification, please report it to [mention contact person/department/number/email] so we can investigate promptly.

Your cooperation in adhering to these guidelines helps ensure the safety and well-being of our entire community. We appreciate your understanding and patience during any power disruptions.

Sincerely,

[Your Name/Management Team]

**URGENT ACTION REQUIRED: Fuel Mixer Replacement Compliance at Spraberry Plant**

This memo provides a critical update on the fuel mixer-to-carburetor replacement project at the Spraberry Plant and outlines immediate steps necessary to ensure regulatory compliance and protect our operations.

**Current Status and Regulatory Requirements**
The Texas Natural Resource Conservation Commission (TNRCC) has conditionally approved our fuel mixer replacement project, recognizing it as a fuel savings initiative with no intended increase in emissions or horsepower. However, their approval is contingent upon our ability to definitively prove these claims through comprehensive before-and-after emissions testing on a representative unit.

**Compelling Business Case for Immediate Action**
I strongly recommend we proceed with this testing immediately for three critical reasons:

1. **Regulatory Compliance Protection**: Failure to complete this testing puts our grandfather status at serious risk. Any violation could result in costly permitting requirements and potential penalties.

2. **Cost-Effective Testing Solution**: I propose using our verified portable emissions tester, which has proven accuracy in side-by-side comparisons with New Mexico units. This approach will save NNG $3,000-$5,000 compared to third-party contractor testing while delivering equally reliable results.

3. **Risk Mitigation**: Testing one unit before full implementation allows us to identify and address any unexpected emissions or horsepower increases before they become plant-wide compliance issues.

**Immediate Action Items**
- TNRCC approval letter being submitted today
- Upon approval, testing must commence immediately
- Exhaust stack sampling ports must be constructed prior to testing
- Only one carburetor installation permitted until testing completion

**Recommendation**
Given the potential financial and regulatory consequences of non-compliance, I urge the team to prioritize this testing initiative. The minimal upfront investment in testing and sampling port construction provides essential protection for our operations and ensures we maintain our competitive advantage through fuel savings while remaining fully compliant.

Please confirm your support for this approach and advise if technical diagrams for sampling port locations are needed.

According to  the TNRCC, they will allow this activity provided that the above is true and  that we prove that emissions and horsepower will not increase.
To do this  they have requested that we conduct an emissions test on one of the units  with the mixer on and then with the carbuerator on as a condition of their  approval.

Subject: Economic Manifesto: Advocating for Strategic Interest Rate Adjustments

Dear Economic Policy Makers and Stakeholders,

We are pleased to present our Economic Manifesto, outlining a critical path towards sustainable economic stability and long-term prosperity. Central to our recommendations is a call for a strategic and measured increase in interest rates.

Our analysis indicates that current economic conditions necessitate a proactive approach to monetary policy. Persistent inflationary pressures are eroding purchasing power, creating uncertainty, and threatening the foundational health of our economy. Raising interest rates is a vital and proven tool to:

1.  **Curb Inflation:** Anchor inflation expectations and bring price stability back into focus, protecting the real value of incomes and savings.
2.  **Promote Financial Discipline:** Encourage more responsible borrowing and lending practices, mitigating the risks associated with excessive debt and speculative activities.
3.  **Strengthen Economic Fundamentals:** Foster an environment where capital is allocated more efficiently, supporting productive investment over unsustainable consumption.

While we acknowledge that such adjustments may present short-term considerations, we firmly believe they are essential for laying the groundwork for enduring economic resilience. This policy move is not merely reactive; it is a forward-looking strategy designed to safeguard the economy against future shocks and ensure equitable, sustainable growth.

We urge all relevant policymakers and economic leaders to carefully consider these proposals and engage in a constructive dialogue towards their implementation. Our shared goal must be an economy built on sound principles, stability, and long-term prosperity for all citizens.

Sincerely,

[Your Name/Organization Name]

Subject: Potential Exposure Calculation Methodology and Collateral Management for Counterparty Risk

Dear Team,

I would like to outline our approach to calculating potential exposure and managing collateral to mitigate counterparty risk.

**Potential Exposure Calculation Methodology:**  
We use a combination of current exposure and potential future exposure (PFE) to assess the total counterparty risk. The PFE is estimated using a Monte Carlo simulation of market variables to project future values of outstanding transactions over the agreed horizon. At each time step, we determine the exposure as the positive mark-to-market value, then calculate the quantile (typically 95th or 99th percentile) to represent potential exposure at a given confidence level. Netting agreements are included where applicable to offset positions with the same counterparty, and we periodically update calculations to reflect market fluctuations and trade lifecycle events.

**Collateral Management:**  
To mitigate counterparty credit risk, we implement collateral agreements (CSA) with counterparties. We perform daily margin calculations to determine required initial and variation margins, based on the mark-to-market value and exposure estimation. Collateral calls are made when exposure exceeds thresholds defined in the CSA. Eligible collateral types, haircuts, and minimum transfer amounts are monitored to ensure compliance and to reduce residual risk. Collateral valuation is updated regularly to account for market changes, and excess/deficit amounts are promptly resolved with counterparties.

Please let me know if you need more details or wish to schedule a meeting to discuss specific counterparty exposures.

Best regards,  
[Your Name]

Frank

USA: INTERVIEW-EnronOnline sees volume growth, CEO says.
By Gelu Sulugiuc  07/17/2001 Reuters English News Service (C) Reuters Limited 2001.
NEW YORK, July 17 (Reuters) - As most players in a shrinking pool of online  energy trading platforms struggle to stay alive, leader EnronOnline has a  simple philosophy: If it ain't broke, don't fix it.
The Internet arm of the energy marketing and trading giant Enron Corp. ,  EnronOnline predicts it will increase its volume and says it can coexist with  the IntercontinentalExchange (ICE), the chief executive of Enron Networks  told Reuters on Tuesday.
The innovative company is always evaluating its business environment, ready  to remold itself according to market demands, but it is not pursuing mergers  or aquisitions for now, according to Greg Piper.
"I would never say never, but we're not proactively looking at aquiring an  ownership position in any other exchange platform," Piper said.
With an average of $3.5 billion in trades every day, EnronOnline enjoys the  highest volume of all energy electronic platforms.
Most energy trading  platforms launched last year have failed to generate profits.
Its closest rival is ICE, which routinely exceeds $1 billion a day.
But while  ICE is a many-to-many exchange that matches bids and offers, on EnronOnline  one can only trade with Enron.
"It's a tool that supercharges our market-making business," Piper said.
Enron is the No.
1 natural gas and electricity marketer in the United States.
About 60 percent of its transactions are captured through the electronic  platform.
"As long as we show good prices to our customers, our volumes will continue  to grow," Piper said.
The company is looking to grow online volume in products such as metals,  steel, weather, petrochemicals and plastics.
"We're trying to remain the leader in energy and help our other markets get  more traction," Piper said.
"There is a huge amount of growth that we haven't  even tapped into yet."
Piper said he is not worried about ICE's recent success.
The Atlanta-based  exchange recently took over London's International Petroleum Exchange and  plans to transfer its open-outcry business online, significantly boosting its  trade volumes.
"Maybe six to 12 months from now, the story might be a lot different," Piper  said.
"But right now, there is room for the both of us."
He added that Enron traders do not shy away from trading on ICE.
Many of the  energy giants that founded ICE and provide most of its liquidity are also  Enron's biggest clients.
"Enron will seek out a good deal on ICE when there is one," Piper said.
INNOVATION KEY TO SUCCESS  Recognized as one of the most innovative companies in the United States,  Enron is constantly evaluating its position in the market and thinking of  ways to become more successful.
"The right thing to do in November 1999 was to launch EnronOnline," Piper  said.
"But we look at it every day and if it made sense to do something  different, you can bet that Enron would do it and we wouldn't be emotional  about it."
One of the company's advantages is the fact that its software is a flexible  application that allows EnronOnline to easily go in an out of different  markets and regions.
It constantly adds new products to its trading arsenal.
But Piper said that EnronOnline has no plans to turn itself in a many-to-many  exchange.
"We want to focus in providing our markets to others," he said.
"In the near  term, we're not changing that."
The company is considering licensing the application itself, but would not  elaborate on who wants it and how much Enron would ask for it.
EnronOnline has been so successful that even its competitors take their hats  off.
"I've been hearing for two years now that a one-to-many exchange wouldn't  work, but Enron just keeps proving people wrong," said Frank Getman, chief  executive of online energy exchange HoustonStreet.
"If you're willing to make tight two-way markets and be the best price in the  market, then people will continue to use your site."
Enron's stock rose 41 cents to $49.53 a share on Tuesday in trading on the  New York Stock Exchange.

Steve Beck

Rick and Greg,

I met with Sally and Beth on August 24th to discuss the operational risk management initiative requiring a reconciliation across all major risk applications.

To make things a bit more engaging, let me share a quick story: During our meeting, Sally recalled an incident from last quarter where a tiny error in transferring data from a risk book to an application went unnoticed. This one slip caused a ripple effect, skewing the VAR calculation for an entire desk. It took the team days to investigate and patch the discrepancy because the exception report hadn’t flagged the error. This experience highlighted how critical a robust reconciliation process is, not just to prevent losses, but to maintain trust in our risk analytics.

This reconciliation is necessary to validate the transfer of all data from source systems, i.e. risk books, into risk applications which calculate VAR, provide credit exposures, feed Infinity with daily cash flows and ultimately the DPR.

Sally and Beth, along with IT, have initiated a project to improve and monitor the accuracy and efficiency of these daily interfaces.

The scope includes a review of the processes which impact the accuracy of information, timing of interfaces, production performance issues, inventory of books and improved controls over changes to book attributes, and the officialization process.

They have agreed to add a requirement to provide, on a daily basis, this reconciliation across all major risk applications.

The projected timeline to complete this project, including the reconciliation initiative, is 60 to 90 days.

We will need to reassess the decision to combine these initiatives, if the GRMO timeline slips.

This daily risk applications reconciliation will provide four key metrics not currently available: 1) the ability to track data "accuracy" in terms of the percentage of information which transferred and processed correctly, vs. just unique "failures". How complete is the data? 2) the ability to validate the accuracy of exception reporting (are all failures included on the exception reports?) 3) the ability to validate Infinity cash flows 4) Reconciliation of values (volumes, PRMA &PRML and cash flows), not # of books processed.

Please call me if you would like to discuss.

Wanda Curry

Subject: Secure On-Air Policy Endorsements

Dear Team,

This email serves as an urgent call to action regarding the strategic importance of securing on-air endorsements for our key policy initiatives. As we enter a critical phase, public validation from influential voices across radio, television, and prominent digital platforms will be instrumental in shaping public opinion and amplifying our message.

Hearing trusted personalities and opinion leaders articulate the benefits and rationale behind our policies can significantly enhance our credibility, expand our reach, and mobilize broader support. We need a concerted, proactive effort to identify potential endorsers who resonate with our objectives and possess a significant platform.

Please prioritize outreach to these targets. The Communications and Policy teams are prepared to provide comprehensive briefing materials, clear talking points, and compelling data to support these discussions. Your role in opening doors and facilitating these crucial conversations is paramount.

Let's work collaboratively to identify opportunities, develop tailored pitches, and secure these vital endorsements. Please provide updates on your progress and any potential leads to [Relevant Contact Person/Department] by the end of this week.

[Your Name/Leadership]
source_text:
We produce political/public affairs television programs which air in state capitols.
Currently we are in Pennsylvania and Ohio, expanding into NJ, Md and DE.
The disruptive technology is this: the real target of the TV show is the guest, not the audience.
Lobbyists have trouble scheduling time with politicians and regulators, and when they get on the schedule lobbyists have time getting genuine intellectual focus from government decision makers.
We don't have trouble with either.
Every politician and appointee wants to be on television, they always say yes.
When they ask us what the topics will be, and we mention something like telecommunications competition or electricity deregulation they want briefing material which they actually study in order to do well on television.
In addition by inviting journalists and radio and television commentators as members of out panel we have the same effect on them.
In short:   Step one: identify gov't decision makers that our sponsors want to influence Step two: invite them on the program and, in doing so, develop rapport with their key staff members on the relevant issues Step three: send briefing materials and/or give a briefing in person before the the taping Step four: towards the end of a show in which the Newsmaker has largely been bragging about his/her policy agenda Step five: steer the conversation to sponsor selected topics, framing the issue in such a way as to make it very difficult for the guest to resist the conclusions suggested by the host.
Step six: take the statement of support for the position we favor e.g.
tort reform, privatization, deregulation, tax cuts, etc.
(which by the way we almost always are able to get from the guest on the air) and in addition to airing along with the airing of the rest of the show, we digitize it and send it out to legislators, regulators and the proper beat reporters via email making it almost impossible for the newsmaker to back off later.
Current sponsors: Medical Society, Hospital Association, State System of Higher Education, Manufacturers Association, Cornell Corrections, AT&T.
Levels: 25K, 50K, 100K per year for Pa; 15k for Ohio (one level only).
This is an amazingly simple, elegant and direct way to influence policy makers and opinion molders and we do not have an energy-oriented firms in partnership with us.
Enron and Newsmakers are a very good fit.
I'll be in touch,   p.s.
Sponsorship can be done in ways that are not visible if you prefer, via intermediaries, if you are publicity shy.
Jerry Bowyer Pennsylvania Newsmakersseen across the state on these television stations: www.jerrybowyer.com/coveragemap.php      The Jerry Bowyer Programon WPTT radio in Pittsburgh, 1360am: www.1360wptt.com/bowyer  Focus on the Issueson Cornerstone Television Audio clips from these programs can be heard at www.jerrybowyer.com/audio.php

Vasant,  A quick update on a number of on-going projects:  1.
JCC Forward Curve/Hedging Strategy (Enron Japan)  h  An update of the historical P&L model was completed and included both commodity and foreign exchange risks.
The standard deviation of historical simulations for single month swaps was significantly reduced with the foreign exchange hedging strategy (two long yen/$ positions and 1 short yen/$ position).
h  Enron Japan, in cooperation with Enron London, developed an alternative hedging strategy based on Brent $ value.
No P&L historical P&L simulations were conducted for the alternative strategy.
h  The original Brent hedge ratios were based on an average of 3 monthly preliminary JCC values offered by METI.
Presumably, the swap will be settled off of the finalized METI JCC price which is released two months after the fact.
Rousseau forwarded those numbers from 1998 to present this morning.
Unfortunately, our model uses historical JCC values going back to August 1991.
Rousseau will hopefully obtain the required historical JCC time series early next week.
h  I haven't yet heard about Jeff Shankman's response to the memo that was forwarded on Wednesday.
2.
Ethanol Forward Curve (Enron Global Markets)     h  A meeting was held with Marc de la Roche, Darren Maloney, and Sanjay Patel to discuss the development of a forward curve for ethanol.
A first-cut curve based on NYMEX unleaded gasoline, NYMEX WTI crude, and EIA fuel ethanol inventories was constructed and backtested.
Rolling monthly backtesting (using data from 2000 to 2001) suggested that, on average, the modeled and actual ethanol prices were off only by a few cents for time periods up to 6 months (e.g., 6 month swap).
Unfortunately, the 1 SD value for the historical projections was quite large (+/- $0.30 on a $1.40/gal commodity).
h The changing dynamics of the ethanol market offer the greatest challenge to forward curve construction.
That is, ethanol will likely replace MTBE as the fuel oxygenate of choice over time, which will probably signal a stronger relationship with unleaded gas price.
Unfortunately, the current model uses historical data from 1998 to present which do not necessarily reflect such a strong relationship.
These concerns have been noted to the ethanol guys.
h  The ENE ethanol pricing index has been updated with August, September, and October prices and continues to generally track other industry publication values (e.g., Oxy-fuel news).
h  Marc and Darren are in talks with Petrous as a potential counterparty for an ethanol swap.
h  An ethanol status meeting will be held Wednesday or Thursday of next week with Randy Maffett.
3.
Plastics Forward Curves (Enron Global Markets)  h  Mauricio Mora and I have focused on the development of forward curves for a suite of plastics including propylene, ethylene, polypropylene, HDPE, and LLDPE (see earlier email for details).
h  Initial models for each of these plastics have been completed and will be compared to the current model forward curves and Alan Engberg's expected values.
Alan did forward the most recent curves and personal outlooks to us today.
h  Note that the methologies behind the creation of the old forward curves are not known.
Evidently, one can use various rankings (say 1 to 5 depending on market conditions) to manipulate the model forward curve--I don't know whether regression was involved in these forward curve constructions.
