Subject: Proposed Bylaw Change Impacting Graduate Membership and Council Composition

Dear Members,

I am writing to inform you of a proposed amendment to our organizational bylaws that would significantly affect both graduate membership requirements and the composition of our governing council.

The proposed changes include:

1. **Graduate Membership Modifications:**
   - Extension of the grace period for transitioning from student to graduate membership from 6 months to 12 months
   - Revised continuing education requirements for graduate members (reducing from 20 to 15 hours annually)
   - Updated fee structure reflecting current economic conditions

2. **Council Composition Adjustments:**
   - Increase in graduate member representation from 60% to 65% of total council seats
   - Addition of two at-large positions specifically designated for recent graduates (within 5 years of graduation)
   - Modification of regional representation to better reflect current membership distribution

These changes aim to enhance graduate member engagement while ensuring robust leadership representation across our diverse membership base. The proposed amendments have been reviewed by the Bylaws Committee and received preliminary approval from the Executive Board.

A detailed summary of the proposed changes will be distributed next week, followed by a 30-day comment period. We encourage all members to review these materials carefully and provide feedback.

The formal vote on these amendments will take place at our Annual General Meeting on March 15th. Members unable to attend in person may vote electronically through our secure member portal.

Please direct any questions or concerns to bylaws@organization.org.

Thank you for your continued engagement in our organizational governance.

Best regards,

[Name]
Secretary, Board of Directors

Gentlemen:  There was a discussion at the Executive Committee meeting last week regarding a bylaw change.
Eliminate existing Bylaw 9 and change it to read that "Members will retain Graduate status for only as long a period as they held Active membership or until normal council retirement at age 72, whichever occurs first."
The following members would be immediately affected by the proposed change and would leave the council:  Sam Armacost, Percy Barnevik, Art Blank, Michael Bonsignore, Ed Budd, Ed Carpenter, David Coulter, Walter Forbes, Jim Johnson, Tim Koogle, Jack Krol, Paul Lego, Jan Leschly, Dick McCormick, Eckhard Pfeiffer, Rick Scott, Pete Silas, Jeff Skilling, Bob Stempel, Rick Thoman, John Walter, Dennis Weatherstone and Bob Winters.
The mandatory retirement provision affects an additional 49 members.
In summary, we currently have 115 Active members and would be reducing the Graduate members from 149 to 77.
Frankly, a more dramatic change than I thought.
Any thoughts?
Phil

John, I met with Sasha today for about 3 hours.
We reviewed the Eterra data entry and trade verification process before sending to QSE MOS.
Here are my suggestions to Sasha for improving Eterra (highest priority first):
- Allow the Deal Entry screen to accept single entry trades (e.g., simultaneous Buy from Calpine (South Zone) and Sell to FPL (North Zone)).
Currently, this requires two entries: a purchase from Calpine (South Zone) to the Hourly Ercot book, and then a sale from the Hourly Ercot book to FPL (North Zone).
Sasha is working on this, but transmission issues between South and North are causing problems.
- Change the Frontera generation increase process.
Currently, a "buy from Frontera" is entered into the Frontera book, which is unintuitive. We're seeking an easier process, perhaps a button to indicate a Frontera purchase, which would increase EPMI mw's in the Ercot Portal.
- Change short names in <internal counterparty> & <external counterparty> to their full names (e.g., "elpasomeren" to "El Paso Merchant Energy").
- Provide a list of Counterparties and their associated QSEs (e.g., El Paso Merchant is APX) to clarify Ercot Portal impacts.
- Automatically update the Contract date to match the flow date, reducing a manual step.
I emphasized to Sasha that in trading, time is critical, and we need a streamlined, user-friendly deal entry process.
The first two items will take time, but the last three should be quick fixes.
I hope this helps.
Joe Capasso

PG&E will announce via press release very early next week an open season on  Redwood, Baja and Silverado.
It comes in direct response to recent announcements of expansions into  California by pipelines.
The bid protocols will be structured similar to original open season from the  original Gas Accord.
The open season will start on June 1 and end on July 31.
Capacity will be available starting 1.1.03.
Bidders will be able to bid up to 30 years (PG&E states that that's what  generators want).
Accompanying the announcement will be another announcement that PG&E will  expand Redwood by 200mmcf/day, which they hope to have available by 1.1.03,  or some time during Q103.
About 2-4 weeks after the open season begins, PG&E will file its proposed  "Gas Accord II,"  (the first one expires end of 02).
As part of that filing, PG&E will offer its proposed ratemaking treatment for  the next five years (beginning 1.1.03).
PG&E will not include in the open season 1) core capacity and 2) certain EAD  contracts that extend beyond the Gas Accord 1 end date.
In addition, PG&E will hold back an additional 20% (after excluding core and  EAD), to be "open-seasoned" at some "future" date.
The capacity to be auctioned is: 1) 900 mmcf/day on Redwood, 2) 245 (annual)  on Baja, plus an additional 200/day in summer on Baja, 3) 155 on Silverado.
How PG&E will market the 20% they intend to hold back, and when they might  auction it off in the future will be discussed in PG&E's Gas Accord II filing.
No single company will be awarded more than 30% of the capacity on any  specific path in the primary open season (though firms can bid whatever level  of capacity they choose).
Please forwad along to anyone else who might be interested.
If you have any  questions, just holler.
Best,

Dear [Recipient Name],

With incumbent Republican Governor Jim Geringer choosing not to seek re-election, the race was wide open. The Republican nominee was Eli Bebout, a prominent figure in the state legislature who served as State Senate President. For the Democrats, the candidate was Dave Freudenthal, a former U.S. Attorney for Wyoming who had previously run for the governorship in 1994.

The contest was closely watched, as Wyoming is historically a very conservative state, making a Democratic victory a significant challenge. However, Freudenthal managed to pull off an upset. He campaigned on a platform that resonated with many voters, emphasizing fiscal conservatism and a focus on state issues.

Ultimately, Dave Freudenthal won the election, defeating Eli Bebout. This victory marked a rare instance of a Democrat winning the governor's office in Wyoming, and he would go on to serve two terms. It demonstrated that even in strong party states, a well-run campaign and a candidate connecting with local concerns can lead to unexpected results.

Best regards,

I'm confident the forthcoming blackline will address these points and help us finalize the agreement.

Hi, Ken:

I'm a former ECT VP who is just down the street, back at Ryder Scott Company—which was my home before my six years with Enron. Those were truly formative years; working on landmark deals like the Dabhol Power Project in India and developing new risk management strategies for natural gas taught me lessons I still draw on today. I thoroughly enjoyed the Company—both the business and the people I worked with, from late nights in the trading pit to strategy sessions with folks like Greg Whalley and Louise Kitchen. Still, there is a sense of satisfaction in returning to the "oil patch"—immersed again in petroleum reserves consulting, seismic data, and old friends at Ryder Scott.

I continue to hold Enron stock and have every intention of remaining a shareholder because I am confident the company will continue to innovate—just as it did with initiatives in broadband, weather derivatives, and power marketing. Enron’s entrepreneurial spirit remains unmatched in the industry, and I believe it will weather current uncertainties.

The reason for my email is to bring to your attention a recent op-ed in the Houston Chronicle, written by Robert Buzzanco, who is, as you may know, a faculty member at the University of Houston. His essay sharply critiqued the current campaign against terrorism, drawing broad, sweeping conclusions that, quite frankly, did not stand up to even basic factual scrutiny. For example, he repeatedly implied that minorities make up a disproportionate share of U.S. military forces, going so far as to assert that minority communities are being unfairly targeted to fill the ranks. However, as a geological engineer—someone whose entire career depends on a rigorous application of data—I find this claim flatly contradicted by readily available Department of Defense statistics: minorities comprise 34.4% of active military personnel, which reflects rather than distorts nationwide demographics and certainly does not support the idea of overwhelming or exploitative minority representation.

Beyond this, Buzzanco’s piece echoed a laundry list of stereotypes about American foreign policy that sounded more like self-promotion for his anti-American books than a serious critique intended to foster debate or peace. Frankly, people like Buzzanco have every right to protest or write opinion columns. Many Americans—including some in our own families—have served, fought, or even sacrificed their lives to defend those rights. Others may have to do so again in the coming months.

However, my objection is that Dr. Buzzanco is leveraging his position at the University of Houston—an institution held in high regard by many in our community, including you—to lend weight and legitimacy to a personal crusade. It’s reminiscent of an Enron employee marching in an anti-globalization rally while wearing the company’s logo and publicly taking sides under the company’s banner, thereby conflating personal viewpoints with the organization's reputation. In the swirling chaos of today’s corporate landscape, the downfall of giants has become a spectator sport for the public and pundits alike. This morning’s Wall Street Journal features a thought-provoking editorial that offers a contrarian take on the latest casualty: Enron.  
Manager's Journal: What Enron Did Right By Samuel Bodily and Robert Bruner  11/19/2001 The Wall Street Journal A20 (Copyright (c) 2001, Dow Jones & Company, Inc.)    This is a rough era for American business icons.
Subject to the vagaries of age (Jack Welch), product failure (Ford/Firestone tires), competition (Lucent, AT&T), technology (Hewlett-Packard and Compaq), and dot-bomb bubbles (CMGI), managers and their firms remind us that being an icon is risky business.
The latest example is Enron, whose fall from grace has resulted in a proposed fire sale to Dynegy.
Once considered one of the country's most innovative companies, Enron became a pariah due to lack of transparency about its deals and the odor of conflicts of interest.
The journalistic accounts of Enron's struggles drip with schadenfreude, hinting that its innovations and achievements were all a mirage.
We hold no brief regarding the legal or ethical issues under investigation.
We agree that more transparency about potential conflicts of interest is needed.
High profitability does not justify breaking the law or ethical norms.
But no matter how the current issues resolve themselves or what fresh revelations emerge, Enron has created an enormous legacy of good ideas that have enduring value.

Pipeline integrity and safety have risen to new levels of public concern.
In the aftermath of the incidents at Bellingham, Washington and Carlsbad, New Mexico new pipeline safety regulations and legislation will require increased focus on pipeline integrity programs.
As a proactive approach to address these concerns, ETS Operations is establishing a Pipeline Integrity Program Management Group.
This group will be responsible for pipeline integrity issues for EOTT and ETS and financial reporting of EOTT's environmental and remediation projects.
The group will include the following functions:  corrosion, pipeline safety and pipeline integrity.
I am pleased to announce that Mike Nelson will relocate to Houston to lead this new initiative, as Vice President Pipeline Integrity Program Management.
Reporting directly to Mike are Max Brown and Dave Johnson.
The establishment of this new function, along with Mike's move, has given us the opportunity to rotate key staff, allowing us to achieve a broader knowledge base for the future of ETS Operations.
I am pleased to announce the following additional changes:                                                                                    Rick Craig - Vice President Southeast Operations                                                                                   Dan Pribble - Vice President Southwest Operations                                                                                  Randy Rice - Senior Director North Operations    Rick Craig and Dan Pribble will continue to office in Houston.
Randy will transfer to the Omaha office.
Don Hawkins will assume new responsibility for controls & electrical, measurement and the Clifton Machine Shop as Vice President Technical Services.
He will also continue to handle facility audits, quality management, and business development initiatives.
John Shafer, Vice President Environmental, Health & Safety, will continue to be responsible for environmental compliance and remediation, and health and safety.
John Keller, Vice President Planning & Power Services, will assume responsibility for the Beaver Machine Shop in addition to his current responsibilities.
Jerry Martin, Vice President Engineering & Construction, will continue in his current role.
The Skill Based Pay Field Training Administration group will now report to Morris Brassfield, Senior Director, Operations Support Services.
All changes will be effective October 1.
Please join me in congratulating these individuals on their new assignments.

Lucy:  Tana tells me you are looking for some guidance as to which Enron entity  should be used for booking trading transactions with various counterparties.
There are a couple of general rules that apply to "normal" trading  circumstances and I'll spell them out below, but remember that these are not  hard and fast rules and may go straight out the window when circumstances  vary (even just a little bit) from "normal."
For example, abnormal  situations exist where the trading transaction is in connection with another  transaction with an Enron company (e.g.
a financing or equity investment),  the counterparty has a legally justifiable desire to trade with a certain  Enron company, the product being traded is only traded by a particular Enron  company or the counterparty is in a jurisdiction outside the country where we  are trading (except as spelled out below).
Having said all that, the  following rules (generally tax driven) can be used as general guidelines:  1.
If there is no master agreement in place between the counterparty and an  Enron company, the trade should be entered into on behalf of the Enron  company based in the country where the Enron trader is when the trade is  concluded and, if there is any hope of further trading with the counterparty,  Credit and Legal should be notified to negotiate a master agreement.
Of  course, if the counterparty is outside the country where we are trading,  Legal should be consulted ahead of time (there are some countries where  derivatives are actually illegal, special procedures must be followed or  can't be done by us from the U.S.).
2.
If there is a master agreement between the counterparty and either ENA or  Enron Canada, and the Enron trader is in the U.S. or Canada, the trade should  be entered into by the trader on behalf of the Enron company that is party to  the master agreement.
If the trader is outside of the U.S. or Canada, other  rules may apply.
3.
If there is a master agreement between the counterparty and ECT  International (usually only European counterparties), and the Enron trader is  in the U.S. or the U.K., the trade should be entered into by the trader on  behalf of ECT International.
Note that there are special considerations if  the trader is in the U.K. based on U.K. regulatory issues (the trade is  actually "arranged" by Enron Europe Finance and Trading Ltd. on behalf of ECT  International).
If such a master exists but the trader is not in the U.S. or  U.K., the trade should be handed off to a trader located in one of those two  countries for final negotiation and execution.
It would be a good idea to  consult with Legal or Tax if this comes up for more specific advice.
These general rules relate to which Enron entity should be the legal  counterparty to the transactions.
This doesn't determine where within the  Enron family the actual risk should ultimately reside.
If we want the risk  to be in an Enron company other than the Enron counterparty for contractual  purposes, an intercompany transaction should be booked (probably through RMT)  to get the risk in the right place.

As an introduction: The referenced counterparty is attempting to resolve the online products it wishes to trade with us (it's accessible for some, but not all of the products it desires to trade).
When I examined Profile Manager to see what they had previously been authorized to trade, I observed that this counterparty was enabled to trade many of the European products, including specifically European physical power products (which is uncommon for a US based counterparty to trade).
Before I proceed to modify the profile for this counterparty, I wanted to verify with you and see if London had specifically enabled them to trade the products they were authorized to trade (especially physical power).
What I typically do when I am authorizing US based counterparties, is that with regard to Non US & Canadian products, as long as they are an Eligible Swap Participant I enable them for all products except European physical power, which I never authorize them for.
Also, Credit Derivatives, I never enable anyone for unless we really intend it.
So, my question to you is did London actively authorize the non US & Canadian based products (especially physical power).
If you didn't, then I am going to treat this as an oversight of the pre-approval process and shut them down for European physical power.

Relative ranking results up through the Senior  Director level are final.
You and your management team can begin the process  of giving performance reviews to your employees.
I spoke with Sheila Walton  today to inquire about an expected time frame for completing and conducting  the employee reviews.
She indicated that the target completion date should  be the end of July.
Promotions will be effective August 1st.
It is Dave Delainey's intent to  announce ENA promotions sometime after he returns from vacation on July 24.
This drives the end of July target completion date for reviews.
I do not  yet know if Delainey wants all ENA promotions to be announced in a single  memo, or if each group within ENA will prepare such a memo.
I will keep you  updated on this as I get direction from him.
Please note the following change since our Energy Operations PRC in June.
In  order to place focus on the qualitative feedback during this mid-year review  process, we will not share performance clusters with employees when  conducting their reviews.
It is very important for all of us to be  consistent in this process, so please communicate this to all in your groups  who will be giving performance reviews.
It is important to note, however,  that the content of an employee's review should be consistent with our view  of that employee's relative ranking.
In other words, an employee in the  Satisfactory category should not be given a review that simply states that  the employee is doing a great job.
Clearly, a large number of employees  performed at a higher level than those employees in the Satisfactory  category, so the feedback to that employee should include some specific areas  of improvement needed in order for the employee to make a stronger impact in  the organization, help you achieve the groups goals, etc.
Also please note the following:   Performance reviews for anyone in the Satisfactory, Needs Improvement or  Issues categories must be reviewed by HR prior to these reviews being given  to the employees.
This will ensure that our feedback is commensurate with  the relative performance of that employee.
(This has been the stated process  for the bottom two categories, and we are adding Satisfactory to this process  as well.)
Please remember to include a more experienced member of your management team,  yourself, or an HR professional in reviews being conducted by inexperienced  members of your management team, or those management team members where you  have a concern over their ability or willingness to deliver candid and  perhaps tough performance feedback.
I believe that we have spent some time  in identifying these situations.
I ask your help to ensure that we follow  through on this commitment.
Thanks for all of your efforts in making this mid-year PRC process a  meaningful one.
It is Dave Delainey's intent to announce It if 0

Andy: In the spirit of "full disclosure", I thought I would let you know what ENA has agreed to on the ISDA side with various Merrill entities.

ENA has ISDA's with Merrill Lynch International Bank (executed 8/25/95 with a $50MM threshold), Merrill Lynch Capital Services Inc. (executed 12/2/92 with automatic termination provisions and a $25MM credit support annex) and Merrill Lynch International (executed 8/25/95 with cross-default language covering parent guarantees).

There is no arbitration provision in any of these agreements; there is merely silence as to jurisdiction with disputes defaulting to New York state courts under New York law (ENA began negotiating mandatory binding arbitration clauses around 1997 following the Amendment to our standard trading documentation).

All of these agreements contain our standard limitation of liability language (in boldface) specifically excluding consequential, punitive, and indirect damages, and capping liability at the notional amount of the underlying transaction, and all permit some type of assignment to an affiliate (in general, without adverse tax consequences under Section 1058 or with sufficient credit support meeting our minimum S&P BBB rating requirement).

All of the agreements provide for setoff rights (including affiliates of non-defaulting parties up to 95% ownership threshold) and all contain standard confidentiality provisions prohibiting disclosure except to regulators, auditors, and legal counsel under attorney-client privilege.

I would therefore propose the following specific changes to Annex I: 
- change the margin deadline time from 2:00 p.m. to 10:00 a.m. (NY time) to align with our London trading desk requirements
- delete Par 9(b) regarding custody arrangements - and you can send your additional no custody required language as a separate side letter
- delete the arbitration provision in Section 12(c) in its entirety including the AAA Commercial Rules reference

I hope that you can respond to the remaining issues (specifically the governing law clause in Section 15 and the event of default threshold in Section 6.3) tomorrow morning so that we can finalize docs by the afternoon and execute before Friday's board meeting.

Thanks for your assistance.
Sara

Business & Finance: ESB Ownership of Network is Questioned – Competition Authority Says Separation of National Grid from Core Company Does Not Go Far Enough

Arthur Beesley reports     11/13/2000  Irish Times  18  Copyright (C) 2000 Irish Times; Source: World Reporter (TM)

The Competition Authority has raised significant concerns about the ESB’s continued ownership of the electricity network in the context of the newly deregulated power market. In a paper submitted to the Department of Public Enterprise, the Authority argues that simply separating the ESB’s National Grid operations from the core company does not sufficiently guarantee fair competition.

According to the Authority, the main issue is that arguments supporting the ESB’s retention of the transmission and distribution system overlook a critical point: a generation company that owns these essential assets “will naturally favour itself” at the expense of both customers and system reliability. Although the Authority's paper has yet to be published, it is believed to state that maintaining both the ESB’s ‘non-competitive’ transmission and distribution assets and its ‘competitive’ electricity generation business is ill-advised from a competition standpoint.

To provide context, the National Grid—which controls the flow of electricity from individual power stations into the network—was separated from the ESB in February when 27 percent of the market was opened to competition. In theory, this separation was meant to ensure that the ESB could not favour its own generation stations over potentially more efficient competitors when managing power flows according to fluctuating demand.

However, the Authority’s response to the Statutory Instrument that facilitated this change—renaming the National Grid as Eirgrid—stated that additional measures are necessary for the market to operate fairly. Some argue that as long as there is an independent operator for the transmission system, ownership could remain with the upstream generator. From this perspective, transferring operational control to Eirgrid would supposedly eliminate any potential discrimination in the scheduling (dispatch) of power and in other operations.

Nevertheless, the Competition Authority contends that this reasoning ignores the strong evidence that a generation company owning transmission lines will “naturally favour itself.” The Statutory Instrument resulted from complex negotiations between the ESB, its trade unions, and the Minister for Public Enterprise, Ms. O’Rourke. Despite the formation of Eirgrid, the ESB retained both ownership and responsibility for developing and maintaining the high-voltage national transmission system, as well as the low-voltage local distribution network.

The Authority, as explained by a person familiar with its paper, recommends that these ownership and maintenance functions should also be separated from the ESB. Such a move is considered necessary to ensure that the competitive market works as intended. By doing so, all electricity generators would have equal access to the power network, receiving objective, transparent, and non-discriminatory treatment.

Finally, the paper highlights that the ESB currently has an incentive to allocate as many costs as possible to the operation of the transmission and distribution system. This practice could further undermine the fairness and transparency of the competitive market.

Here is a brief summary of the environmental findings identified during the records review conducted at the Corpus Christi Koch facility offices on May 1st and 2nd of this year.

All available environmental records in the file data room at the Koch office were reviewed. It was assumed that these records were complete for all assets included in the sale. The review focused primarily on environmental issues typically associated with the sale or purchase of assets involved in the distribution and transmission of crude oil, with particular attention given to pipelines and tank farms, which were considered the most critical assets.

Based on the data reviewed, the Koch assets were found to be in compliance with the following:

- Air permitting, permit by rule, standard exemptions, recordkeeping, and fee payments were all documented.
- NSPS recordkeeping and inspections for VOC control on large crude oil tanks were documented.
- Oil Pollution Act (OPA 90) plans had been prepared and were up to date.
- SARA compliance and reporting requirements had been met.
- SPCC plans had been prepared for each site required under 40 CFR 112.
- Spill reporting history and notifications to the state agency were available for review.
- Ongoing groundwater and soil remediation activities are underway at one site included in the asset sale, with proper permits in place.
- Hazardous waste notifications, annual reports, and fee payments were documented.

Based on this review, no major environmental limitations or liabilities were identified. This conclusion is based on the assumption that all relevant environmental information for the assets in question was present in the data room. 

It should also be noted that this analysis of Koch's environmental compliance assumes that Koch has not withheld, falsified, or misrepresented any information or knowledge during their presentation or in the facility files.

Should there be further development or continued interest in this potential purchase, it is recommended that a Phase I due diligence and site visit be conducted at each location to verify the findings from the records review. Additionally, due to Koch’s operating history, it is recommended that contract conditions explicitly state that EOTT will not be held liable for any discoveries of past deficiencies or releases of contamination that may have occurred on any of the Koch assets being purchased.

Dan,  I have reviewed the Wildhorse (Mesa) Gathering, Processing, and  Transport Agreement.
This agreement is still valid and the gas is dedicated  to this Agreement through 2013.
The agreement present some problematic  issues which I will outline.
1.
Gas Quality -  The gas quality provisions only require Wildhorse to  transport the gas if the gas meets the downstream carriers (in this case  Northwest Pipeline) gas quality specifications.
We propose to put in a  treating plant which would allow the gas to meet the specifications, however  there are no provision in this Agreement which allow us to insert a plant  between Northwest Pipeline and Wildhorse.
Wildhorse could delay are extract  value from us for this connection.
This is an uncertainty.
2.
Wildhorse Obligation to Perform - Based on my understanding of the  facts, at some point during the term of this agreement, Northwest Pipeline  enforced their gas quality specifications and refused to take the gas at the  downstream side of Wildhorse's Gathering System.
As a result, Wildhorse shut  in Enogex's production and it has been shut in ever since.
Wildhorse has a  right to do this under this Agreement (see #1 above) and therefore Wildhorse  has not breached its obligation to transport under this Agreement.
Wildhorse's obligation was suspended when Northwest refused receipt of the  gas.
3.
Unprofitability - Assuming Wildhorse worked with us to install the  treating plant which conformed the gas to Northwest Specifications, they  could refuse to provide gathering service under this agreement if it was  still uneconomical for them to do so.
If they decided it is uneconomical for  them to do so, they have the right to provide Enogex with various potential  solutions which include (i) renegotiating the terms (ii) allowing Enogex to  operate Wildhorse's equipment at Enogex sole cost, expense and risk, or (iii)  release the gas from the Agreement.
The problem here is that there is no  time limit under which Wildhorse must reach a solution with us and no  specific solution they must reach.
Wildhorse could drag this out for some  extended period of time and they could extract significant value.
My  recommendation is that we make Enogex's resolution of these issues with  Wildhorse a condition precedent to closing and funding this deal.
I know the  timing is late.
However if Enron funds this deal and takes on the risk of  negotiating with Wildhorse to resolve either a new deal or a release of the  gas,  everyone needs to understand that such negotiation could take  substantial time and Wildhorse will have significant leverage.
Let me know if you wish to discuss this further or have any questions.

Pressure Requirements: According to the Mitsubishi 501F technical specifications, the required pressure at the inlet is 530 psi, not accounting for system losses. Therefore, the required delivery pressure from FGT's mainline should be 560 psi to ensure sufficient supply after losses.

Hourly Gas Requirements: While we have considered various turbine configurations, the hourly natural gas requirement for the project has remained consistent at approximately 2,100 MMBtu/hr, assuming a 16-hour-per-day operating cycle.

Looping vs. Lateral: We are prepared to follow FGT’s recommendation in this regard, provided that a single meter configuration is utilized instead of a dual configuration.

Phase VI Strategy: The strategy is either to include this construction within the Phase VI expansion (with this being the initial component launched to meet our time constraints), or to have it executed under FGT’s regular construction blanket.

FGT Deadline: To my understanding, FGT must finalize the Phase VI plans by April 30, 2001.

These are the main points as they currently stand. Should you or anyone else have comments, questions, or suggestions, please feel free to reach out.

Thank you,

Dear Ken,  Today I learned that effective midnight tonight I have been made redundant from my position in Enron Europe.
I have worked for Enron for the last 10 years and I can say that despite what has happened today, joining Enron was the best career move I made.
The past 10 years have presented opportunities that were beyond my wildest dreams.
I appreciate everything that Enron has done for myself and my family, and I leave believing that I did my best to return my gratefulness in some way.
While growing up in a worling class environment my father taught me two great lessons in life, which I believe we all need to learn.
The first being that if you ever want anything in life then you had better work for it.
The second being that you should never understand the meaning of the word "can't".
I believe that I have been able to follow his teaching in my career with Enron.
I leave Enron with tremendous experience and, most of all a feeling of belonging to something that was once great.
I truly believed in the company and its people.
Indeed I have reminded myself daily over the last few weeks that Enrons success was built more on its intangible assets rather than its tangible assets.
Enron's greatness was built by its people because we all have dreams and ambitions to be a part of something great.
Although I leave the company with great sadness I also leave with a great feeling of thanks and appreciation.
Arthur Ransome

**FERC Draft Orders Issued Today**

**NYISO TEP and Bid Cap (ER01-3001):** 
FERC approved NYISO's request to extend the current $1,000/MWh bid caps on certain NYISO-administered markets and extend its Temporary Extraordinary Procedures (TEP) for Correcting Market Design Flaws and Addressing Transitional Abnormalities until the Northeastern RTO becomes operational. However, FERC ordered NYISO to narrow the TEP scope and file revised tariff sheets within 30 days.

**NYISO Virtual Bidding Procedures (ER01-3009; ER01-3153):** 
FERC approved tariff changes implementing virtual bidding, which will allow market participants to submit non-physical generation and load bids into the day-ahead market and settle these bids in the real-time market. FERC also accepted NYISO's Market Mitigation Measures designed to address potential gaming or market power strategies arising from virtual bidding.

**NYISO Interconnection Cost Responsibility (ER01-2967):** 
FERC approved tariff changes allocating interconnection costs as follows:
- Developers pay 100% of costs for facilities necessary to physically interconnect their projects
- Developers pay for transmission system upgrades required solely due to their interconnection, minus costs for facilities that NYISO's regional plan determines would be necessary for load growth and reliability regardless of the interconnection

**ISO-NE Interim Bid Caps (ER01-3086):** 
FERC approved extending bid caps until the Northeastern RTO becomes operational.

**Calpine v. ISO-NE (EL01-124):** 
FERC granted the complaint filed by Calpine and Mirant, finding that ISO-NE violated a Commission order by amending Market Rule 5 to exclude external contracts from setting the energy clearing price.

For additional information, contact Susan Lindberg at x30596.

So Burton hits me with, "I hear you drink like a fish. Supposedly you were slamming them back last night." The way he said it, half laughing, made it sound like this was a well-known fact, not just idle gossip. Immediately, I wondered where on earth he could have gotten such a colorful description—especially given that I was at the house the night before with only a few people present and definitely wasn’t making a spectacle of myself. When I pressed him, he replied nonchalantly, "From our friend on 28." This wasn’t just any acquaintance; this was someone I’d confided in before, someone who I didn’t think would be so quick to spread rumors or exaggerate things for a laugh. 

To set the record straight—or perhaps just to call out the absurdity—I fired off a pointed message to our mutual friend: "Nice... so do you inform everyone you come in contact with that I drink like a fish?" I waited for a reply, expecting maybe a sheepish apology, or at least a justification. Instead, radio silence. Not so much as a typing bubble. What happened next was even more telling: instead of answering me, he dialed up Burton, furious that Burton had “ratted him out.” It was like watching a rerun of some juvenile blame game, except these are grown adults.

Here’s where it gets interesting—the reaction speaks volumes. If he truly didn’t care about me or what I was up to, why did he go out of his way to defend himself, to lash out at Burton for merely revealing his role? This isn't the behavior of someone who's indifferent; it’s the reaction of someone who's invested in the narrative, in how he's perceived, and especially, in keeping tabs on me. It’s a pretty clear pattern: this is the same guy who, even after asserting he’s moved on, still brings up references to my supposed habits in conversation, just subtle enough to sound casual, but pointed enough to let me know he’s watching.

And so the eternal question remains: if you’re truly no longer interested, why care so much? Why monitor, repeat stories, and get defensive when called out? The evidence keeps stacking up—and with each move, what’s left unsaid becomes even more compelling.

Maybe this should be on the list for our 300 meeting, along with the related issues of backup power arrangements and emergency supply protocols.

Kay

Apologies for the fact that they are quick and dirty.
All Enron's public statements that I have read, including, I think, statements made to financial analysts, state that our exposure in California is not "material." For instance, in the last quarterly earnings call and in several press releases over the past year, the company has consistently categorized California-related risk as relatively minor, using language such as "manageable" or "not significant."
Dennis' declaration, however, says that the situation in California has been a "financial disaster," that "Enron has lost over $300 million," and that "Enron stands to lose millions more." These losses are described as "huge." This language is much stronger and more alarming than anything previously stated publicly. Moreover, financials provided at investor conferences have typically downplayed California-driven losses and emphasized strong risk management practices. If Dennis’ figures are accurate, that's a substantial discrepancy. I recall several analyst reports as recently as last month citing Enron’s official position that exposure was capped and losses would be limited compared to peers, which contrasts sharply with assertions of ongoing and possibly increasing losses. Perhaps this is information that has since been communicated to the market, but I'm not aware of it. And if it hasn't, it could represent a significant conflict with previous statements and could potentially raise questions from investors, the SEC, or the media about our prior disclosures.
Seems prudent to run this by IR, legal, and perhaps others before releasing. Given the potential implications, it may also be worth coordinating with regulatory affairs and compliance teams to ensure accuracy and consistency with any recent external filings or regulatory submissions.
Regarding the statements about our hedging strategy. It would seem prudent to run this through the organization for comment and discussion prior to making public, especially considering that our hedging practices have been the focus of questions at recent analyst meetings and that misstatements here could have broader ramifications for stakeholder confidence. Several recent news articles have specifically referenced our hedging policies in the context of California, so any inconsistencies could become a flashpoint.

The crisp scent of approaching winter fills the air as light rain is expected to develop over Southeast Texas late tonight or early Tuesday, pattering softly against windows and creating the earthy smell of wet pavement.

The rain may be mixed initially with snow...sleet or freezing rain along and north of a line from Lake Livingston to Brenham, creating an icy tapping sound on rooftops and the metallic tang of frozen precipitation in the air.

Cold air will drain southward with a biting sharpness that stings exposed skin as the precipitation continues to develop...and a changeover to snow or sleet is expected during the day Tuesday, blanketing the region in hushed silence broken only by the gentle crunch underfoot.

Precipitation could change to snow or sleet even as far south as metro Houston by days end Tuesday or early Tuesday evening, transforming familiar landscapes into a white wonderland that muffles sound and fills the air with the clean, crisp smell of fresh snow.

Exact snow and sleet amounts are difficult to pinpoint at this time, but especially north of Houston, two inches or more could accumulate by the time the precipitation tapers off late Tuesday night, creating a soft, pillowy texture that yields beneath footsteps with satisfying squeaks and crunches.

Temperatures will be right around the freezing mark tomorrow over northern sections of the watch area, bringing air so cold it burns the lungs and turns breath into visible puffs of vapor in spots such as Crockett, Huntsville, and College Station.

Motorists should be alert for deteriorating driving conditions tomorrow and tomorrow night, as tires lose their familiar grip on asphalt that becomes slick and treacherous to the touch. Even in metro Houston, driving could become dangerous, with the normally smooth hum of tires on pavement replaced by the unsettling sensation of sliding and the acrid smell of brakes working harder than usual, especially tomorrow night when temperatures fall below freezing.

Any liquid left on roads will freeze with the crystalline hardness of glass, especially on lightly travelled secondary roads where the silence is broken only by the occasional crack of ice expanding.

The system is fast moving and should be east of the area by Wednesday morning, leaving behind the fresh, washed scent of cleared air.

Temperatures will rise above freezing over the entire area Wednesday, bringing the gentle dripping sounds of melting snow and sleet as accumulated winter precipitation transforms back to water that gurgles down gutters and drains.

Very cold temperatures are expected Wednesday night, when the air becomes so frigid it seems to crack with each breath and the silence is profound. Any wet areas left on roads will freeze hard as glass with the sharp sound of expanding ice as temperatures fall into the 20 to 25 degree range inland, where the cold penetrates through layers of clothing to chill bone-deep.

You may wish to consider making preparations to wrap exposed pipes with the rough texture of insulating materials and arrange for pets and portable plants to be brought inside where the warmth carries the comforting scents of home heating and shelter.

A winter storm watch means winter weather is possible...not a certainty, though the anticipation hangs in the air like the metallic scent before a storm. If winter weather becomes imminent, bringing with it the muffled quiet of heavy snowfall and the sharp bite of freezing air, a winter storm warning or winter weather advisory will be issued.

Avoid driving if winter weather becomes imminent, when roads become treacherous sheets of ice that offer no grip and the world transforms into a crystalline landscape where every surface gleams with dangerous beauty.

Dear [Recipient’s Name],

I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to request your support for Houston’s bid to host the 2012 Olympic Games. As you may know, bringing the Olympics to Houston would not only showcase our city on an international stage, but also provide tremendous economic, cultural, and social benefits to our community.

Your support is vital to the success of our bid. We would greatly appreciate your assistance in promoting Houston’s candidacy and helping us demonstrate the city’s enthusiasm and capability to host this prestigious event.

Ken,  Houston's bid for the 2012 Olympic Games is entering the final phase of the domestic bid process.
This summer, the United States Olympic Committee (USOC) will conduct initial site visits and evaluations of the eight U.S. bid cities with the goal being to cut the number of cities to three or four.
This cut will occur in December of this year.
The USOC will be conducting Houston's site visit July 16-19, 2001.
This site visit is critical to our ultimate success in bringing the Olympic Games to Houston.
Over the four-day period in which the USOC site evaluation team is in Houston, two days will be devoted to venue tours and presentations.
There are eight presentation topics predetermined by the USOC, one of which is International Strategy.
Simply stated, this is where we show why we think Houston can win on the international level.
As a Port Commissioner and a board member of Houston 2012, I will be part of the team that presents this section to the USOC site evaluation team.
As arguably the most identifiable international corporate leader in Houston and as the Chairman of the 1990 Economic Summit and the 1992 Republican National Convention, both of which you left with a positive surplus (very important to the Olympics), you are in an excellent position to discuss Houston's international status.
George DeMontrond, Susan Bandy (the Houston 2012 Exec Director) and I would very much appreciate 15 minutes or so of your time to update you on Houston's bid efforts and discuss your potential participation in the upcoming site visit.
You are our first and only choice, and I'd like the opportunity to show you how important this is for Houston.
We expect the number of U.S. bid cities to be reduced to four finalists by this December as a result of these meetings.
I will call Rosalee to schedule a time for a visit at your offices.
All the best and I look forward to catching up with you soon.
I'm attaching my bio, which details the last few years of activity I've been involved with, most of which emanated from your support for me on the UH Board of Regents, the 1990 Economic Summit Host Committee, the 1992 RNC Convention and later the GHP.
Thank you for everything you've done for Sarah and me -- hopefully I've reciprocated by doing a good job for you each

Rick, this memo summarizes the key outcomes of my budget meeting with Michael on Wednesday.
I will forward the complete budget package separately, but these are the critical highlights: While constructive, Michael has issued unequivocal cut demands across other groups.

The original (adjusted) 2001 headcount budget was 52. Michael is now demanding a freeze at the current 44. This freeze necessitates:
*   Not replacing recent departure: Karin Levin.
*   Cancelling scheduled Houston rotation: Oliver Harrison.
*   Halting all scheduled new arrivals: John Collenette, Karl Sees, Blair Van Zant, Adam Bauer, Michel Gantois, Tracy Ngo.
    (This 44 figure includes 5 new hires onboarded last month.)

Despite the reduced headcount, the projected 2002 budget is significantly larger than 2001 due to:
*   A $1.6MM increase from full costing of expats (salary plus 4x salary, instead of just salary).
*   A $500k allocation for communications.
*   An increase in benefit costs from 10% to 23%.
    (Note: All other expenses have been lowered, but the budget remains unfinalized.)

Michael specifically requested the following:
*   Reduce Travel budget by a significant amount (targeting approximately $100k reduction).
*   Provide more precise justification for RAC Corp allocations:
    *   Credit: $350k appears low (including roles for you, Bill, Debbie, credit reserve, CAS).
    *   Market: $660k is considered high/acceptable.
    *   Underwriting: $499k is deemed too high.
    *   Portfolio: $108k requires further clarification.
*   Prepare for potential headcount reductions under two scenarios:
    *   a) 5 heads
    *   b) 10 heads

A 5-head reduction could be accommodated with minimal service impact, *provided* we continue to divest 'operational' credit responsibility *and* maintain the current low volume of large underwritten transactions and revaluations. Specific coverage gaps and weaknesses will remain: EBS, a German-speaking credit specialist, insufficient depth in international markets, and limited market risk management expertise.

A 10-head reduction would be highly disruptive. My strong recommendation is to fundamentally re-assess RAC's role, focusing on significantly less process-oriented work and establishing clear accountability to mitigate blame.

Final budget approval is contingent upon the completion of a comprehensive business review over the coming few weeks.
I suggest we discuss these points next week once you have had a chance to review.
Ted

The value in the remaining coal, supported by puts and fixed price arrangements, is in excess of $25 million.

Jeff,

I am Dr. Mona Yousry. We haven't met, but I earned my Ph.D. in Mathematics in 1982 and have since served 19 years in the telecommunications industry. My career includes recruitment by Bell Laboratories, AT&T, Ameritech, and Sempra Energy.

I have always been impressed by Enron's performance and business strategies. I believe you were instrumental in shaping Enron into what it is today.

I recently read an article about your zealous interest in Africa, and it immediately brought someone to mind. You need to meet Larry Robinson. The following is in his own words. Please read it.

Mona

Lawrence Robinson: Born in Congo, Central Africa, 1952.

My father was born in Zimbabwe. My parents and grandparents were missionaries; my grandparents traveled from California to Africa in 1912 and are both buried there.

I was raised in very remote areas of the Belgian Congo. From an early age, I spent extensive time in the African Bush, learning many secrets necessary to survive — and love — it. I had the opportunity to study and learn animal behavior in ways most experts only dream about.

Some of my greatest memories involve taking a pocket full of salt with my rifle and going into the bush for 10 days to 2 weeks at a time, sometimes totally alone. This was also how I learned about the African people, their languages, and cultures.

As time passed and Independence swept the continent, I saw Zaire, the great land where I was born, turn into a bloodbath. There, witnessing men slaughter men, women, and children, I learned more about the most savage creature of all. It also gave me a profound understanding of how organized and balanced nature truly is.

I am a U.S. Citizen and a resident in Tanzania, East Africa. I am tri-lingual and understand three other African languages. I hold an FAA Commercial Pilot's license.

My education spans institutions in Cape Town, South Africa; Singapore; Beirut, Lebanon; Michigan; and California. I hold two B.S. degrees, one in Agriculture and one in Industrial Education.

I have traveled the world many times. My longest overland trip was a 10-month, 30,000-mile journey from Germany to Cape Town in my own Toyota Land Cruiser. Crossing the Sahara and Kalahari Deserts before GPS was available was truly a great adventure.

From 1985 to 1992, I owned and operated my import-export company in Central Africa, "Malaika Zaire."

Presently, I am Managing Director and Chairman of the Board for "Solar Universal Network" (S.U.N.), a Californian Non-profit Organization, 501(c)3. S.U.N. has also been established in Tanzania as an International NGO since 1995.

- Full utilization of the company's revolving credit facility
- Continued rating agency scrutiny and potential downgrade concerns

Enron taps credit line; stock slides  10/27/2001 Associated Press Newswires  Copyright 2001.
The Associated Press.
All Rights Reserved.
HOUSTON (AP) - After Enron Corp. tapped into more than $3 billion in credit in an effort to boost confidence of investors and customers, stock prices dropped.
Enron Corp.'s stock price hit its lowest point in more than five years Friday.
Shares fell 95 cents on Friday to $15.40, a level not seen since 1995, as analysts continued to muddle through a complicated series of bookkeeping issues revealed after the company's earnings announcement earlier this month.
The stock is down more than 50 percent in two weeks, and the company lost almost $14 billion in market value.
Late this week the company decided to convert $3 billion in revolving credit it has through various banks into cash.
The company put about $1.1 billion in the bank in an effort to reassure business partners and investors of its liquidity and is using the $2.2 billion balance to begin an orderly repurchase of a certain kind of short-term corporate IOU known as commercial paper.
"Nothing spells confidence quite like cash, which is what we want investors to understand," said Enron spokesman Mark Palmer of the $1.1 billion banked this week.
Palmer could neither confirm nor deny that the company is negotiating further lines of credit with banks but described such actions as "good management decisions."
On Oct. 16 Enron's third-quarter earnings release drew renewed attention to an issue investors and analysts had previously been unhappy about: Then-Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow, with the Enron board's approval, had formed and run two investment partnerships that could have created a conflict of interest.
The partnerships, LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, did complex financing and hedging deals with Enron.
Fastow had resigned from his roles in the partnerships months ago when Wall Street began to question whether he could watch out for the interests of Enron's shareholders and the investment partnership simultaneously.
But last week when the company reported a $35 million loss related to ending its LJM ties as well as a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, new questions began to arise.
The Securities and Exchange Commission's Division of Enforcement launched an informal inquiry into the partnerships, and earlier this week Fastow was put on a leave of absence.
Reducing the company's debt exposure through commercial paper and putting it back into more traditional financial tools, like a revolving line of credit, could give great peace of mind to Enron's investors, said Anatol Feygin, an analyst with J.P. Morgan.
"It helps them shore up their support behind their energy trading business, which is really the core of their operations," Feygin told the Houston Chronicle for Saturday's editions.
Carol Coale, an analyst with Prudential Securities, still sees the move as somewhat confusing.
"Just last week they were touting their unused lines of credit as a plus, but the fact that they tapped those now sends a strange, mixed message," she said.
"Do they need the cash to keep the rating agencies off their back?
Is it a gesture for customers?
It first struck me as another one of these strangely timed actions on the part of management."

Attorney Work Product/Not Discoverable  Top Legal Risks  1.
Power Forms -  Trading contracts in the power industry are very weak.
Common problems include trading under multiple masters, no penalty payments for non-delivery, no events of default or calculation of termination damages, broad performance outs.
2.
Agency - Several of our major trading partners operate through an agent acting on behalf of several operating companies.
This creates uncertainty about which entity is liable for which trades.
3.
Municipalities - Difficult authorization issues with municipalities.
4.Complexity of transactions - Power transactions can be very complex due to difficult delivery mechanics and volatile pricing.
5.Timing of transactions - Power transactions typically must be completed on a very tight time schedule.
6.
Lawyer Training - Difficult, time consuming process to train lawyers on how to document transactions involving power.
7.Process for approval of transactions - Uncertain procedures for making sure everybody understands risks associated with transactions.
Documentation Projects  1.
EEI - continued work to make EEI the trading contract for power/lessen reliance on WSPP.
2.
One-off Power Form - creation of contract to be used for individual transactions that are not part of a master.
3.
Product Definition - continued work on creating/building acceptance for power product definitions.
4.
Platform Trading - Encourage use of EEI as trading platform for all e-trading.
5.
Single master contract for all physical commodities/financial trading - work with ISDA to develop single contract for physical trading and then roll that into single contract for physical and financial trading

I talked with Julie Smith right after lunch about ENA responding to Tennessee's South Texas Expansion.
The deadline to submit a response is this afternoon at 5:00 pm with the understanding that a binding precedent agreement with termination outs needs to be executed by tomorrow afternoon (i.e.
Thursday, November 29th).
I told Julie that I thought it was best if ENEL, rather than ENA, submitted the open season response and signed Tennessee's PA.  That way ENEL's RFP response would not get snarled up with any credit concerns that Tennessee had with the Enron Corp. announcements.
I told her that we were still an on-going concern and still wanted to sell gas to the project.
She appreciated our honesty and reaffirmed that ENEL was still interested in entering into a fuel supply arrangement with ENA.
Also, I just received an announcement from Rio Bravo Pipeline that said that "due to the CFE changing the date on which the bidders must present their Bid Proposals for the Rio Bravo IV Project from December 4, 2001 to December 11, 2001" that the Rio Bravo Pipeline Open Season was also being pushed back to December 7, 2001.
So it looks like ENEL has about another week to work on their proposal.
Ruth  P.S.
I just got off the phone with Tennessee Gas Pipeline to thank them for extending the Open Season for us and give him an update on participating in the expansion.
He indicated that "another international company" had just submitted an Open Season response.
So it looks like ENEL has submitted the necessary paperwork.

Your opportunity to register for the invitation-only Neptune Regional Transmission System Open Season Pre-Bid Conferences is running out.

NeptuneRTS, the FERC-approved subsea HVDC electric transmission system that will interconnect Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Maine and New Jersey to downtown Boston, New York City, Long Island, and the Connecticut shore, will begin its initial sale of Transmission Scheduling Rights on September 10.

In advance of that opportunity, NeptuneRTS and its advisors from Skadden Arps, Societe Generale, and Energy Security Analysis will hold pre-bid conferences as follows:

September 5 – Houston, Texas: Under the gleam of downtown high-rises, industry leaders will gather in a glass-walled conference room, sunlight spilling across polished tables as participants pore over transmission maps spread between laptops and legal pads.

September 6 – Halifax, Nova Scotia: Attendees will ascend the steps of a historic waterfront hotel, where blue-gray light from the harbor filters into an airy ballroom echoing with quiet anticipation and the low hum of side conversations about cross-border energy markets.

September 7 – New York City: In a sleek Midtown boardroom above the city’s relentless bustle, the skyline visible through panoramic windows, conferees will sip coffee as legal teams shuffle thick binders and financial advisors confer in low tones.

If you are one of the many participants who have already registered, you can expect your confirmation card in the mail this week.

If you have not yet registered, please do so with Paul Rich at (207) 487-4183 or by email at prich@neptunerts.com. A conference agenda is attached.

If you have not received a copy of the Neptune Bidders Brochure, you may also request one by e-mail.

We look forward to seeing you next week!

- Open Season Pre-bid Agenda 28Aug01.doc

**URGENT REMINDER**                    
**Re: October 1, 2001 ICAP Strip Auction - Credit Requirements**  

In order to participate in the October 1, 2001 Strip Auction to procure Installed Capacity (ICAP) for the six month capability period of November 1, 2001 through April 30, 2002, please be reminded of the following critical requirements:  

**1. COLLATERAL SUBMISSION DEADLINE**
To ensure that your bid will be considered in the auction process, collateral consisting of NYISO approved letter of credit, surety bond or corporate guarantee must be received by the NYISO by **September 24, 2001 at 5:00 PM EST**. Late submissions will result in automatic disqualification from the auction.

**2. EXPIRATION DATE REQUIREMENTS**
This financial instrument must have an expiration date no earlier than **June 30, 2002**. This extended timeframe allows for a two-month buffer beyond the capability period end date to accommodate potential settlement and payment processing delays.

**3. COLLATERAL AMOUNT SPECIFICATIONS**
The collateral amount must equal or exceed the maximum potential financial exposure based on your intended bid quantities and the historical price cap of $8.00/kW-month for ICAP. For example, if bidding on 100 MW of capacity, minimum collateral should be $4,800 (100 MW × $8.00/kW-month × 6 months).

**4. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS**
This collateral should be sent via certified mail or hand-delivered to the attention of:                 
Michael Mackles, Credit Manager                
NYISO, Inc.                
290 Washington Avenue Extension, Suite 300                
Albany, NY 12203
Phone: (518) 356-6000
Email: MMackles@nyiso.com

**5. ACCEPTABLE COLLATERAL FORMS**
- **Letters of Credit**: Must be issued by banks with minimum S&P rating of A- or Moody's rating of A3
- **Surety Bonds**: Must be issued by surety companies rated A- or better by A.M. Best
- **Corporate Guarantees**: Available only for entities with investment grade credit ratings (BBB- or higher)

**6. AUCTION SPECIFICATIONS**
The October 1st auction will procure capacity for NYCA zones A through K, with separate clearing prices for each zone. Historical clearing prices have ranged from $2.50/kW-month to $7.85/kW-month depending on zone and season.

For questions regarding credit requirements, contact the Credit Department at (518) 356-6060. For auction procedures, contact Market Operations at (518) 356-6070.

Dear Team,

I am reaching out to highlight several security concerns that have come to my attention within our organization. It is critical that we address these issues promptly to maintain the integrity and confidentiality of our operations.

Recently, there have been instances of unauthorized access to sensitive information and lapses in following proper security protocols. These incidents put both our data and our reputation at risk. Please treat this matter with the utmost urgency. Let’s work together to strengthen our security practices and protect Enron’s interests.

If you have questions or need clarification on security protocols, please contact the IT security team.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Best regards,

Charlene:  Outlined below are the points I promised to send you before our  meeting on Wednesday morning.
I don't know your agenda for the meeting, so  it may or may not be appropriate to discuss all of these items tomorrow.
Background:  As a long-time supporter of the analyst program, I became  concerned over the last several months as frustration emerged from other  supporters of the program.
Many of those expressing frustration are heavily  involved in the recruiting process.
It is their commitment to both  recruiting and providing analyst rotations that has been key in attracting  talented candidates to what has been the Merchant Services Analyst Program.
I initiated a meeting, announced at Rick Causey's staff meeting, that would  bring us together so that we could consolidate our concerns and then discuss  them with you in a constructive manner.
Our intent is continued support and  improvement of the program.
The meeting took place on March 28 and included  the following:   Brenda Herod   ENA - Energy Operations Executive Lead - LSU   Brent Price  ENA - Energy Operations Executive Lead - UT     Jeff Sommers  CALME    Executive Lead - Univsersity of Florida   Ed Coats  Corp. Tax    Core Team Member - UT, A&M, LSU and University of  Florida   Sally Beck  ENA - Energy Operations Executive Lead - UT and OU   Carolyn Barrett  EBS       Howard Selzer  Enron Global E&P    Summary of Concerns and Discussion Points:  One program, or two:  Prior to campus recruiting in the fall 1999, an  announcement  was made that there would be one analyst program.
Not much  materialized from that point to clarify what that meant or how that would be  managed.
In fact, those of us involved heavily in the recruiting process saw  that the MSAP and the Commercial Anlayst programs were managed separately and  differently in terms of campus recruiting, rotations and orientation.
We  feel uninformed and therefore are hampered in discussing the analyst program  on campus.
SIngle start date:  The single start date of July 17 for analysts is  impractical and inflexible; a concern from our points of view for an  innovative company.
The July start date does not consider December graduates  and is not necessarily practical for undergrads whose graduation dates are in  May.
Lack of communication:   We are some of the most involved and committed  senior managers in the MSAP, and yet we have received little information or  communication about the program.
We hear rumors of "tracks", but no facts  or details.
Some of us had heard about the single July start date, and some  had not.
Commercial focus too heavy:  Presentation materials, the attitudes of support  staff in the Associates/Analysts Program and interview processes are heavily  focused on commercial needs, without understanding support needs.
Lack of input from biggest supporters:  Given the time and effort that many  of us put into the MSAP, we are concerned that we haven't been asked to join  with you in some of your plans for the program.
We are concerned that  decisions (example:  the single start date) are being considered in a vacuum  without what could be some valuable input from some of us.
MSAP has taken a step backward:  Previously, with a dedicated leadership team  and staff, the MSAP had made great strides in the consistency of our on  campus efforts, the quality of candidates, the acceptance rate of top  candidates and the pride of participants in the program.
We feel that the  focus on the MSAP has diminished considerably over the last nine months, and  we are anxious to work with you to renew excitment for the program.
Summary Concerns/Discussion Points:  Disc

The CPUC has postponed its decision on authorizing a 15% payment to qualifying facilities (QFs) for their outstanding debt. Industry sources attribute this delay to several factors: concerns that such payments might constitute preferential treatment during potential bankruptcy proceedings (an issue the PUC must consider given current market conditions), and uncertainty about implementation procedures for the proposed 15% payment.

This postponement reflects the PUC's typical decision-making approach and comes at a time when both Southern California Edison and PG&E face numerous financial obligations competing for their cash resources.

The proposal to pay QFs 15% of owed amounts also presents legal complications, as it would involve settling debts with select creditors while leaving others unpaid. Such selective payment arrangements could prompt non-QF creditors to pursue involuntary bankruptcy proceedings against Southern California Edison.
source_text:
CPUC Delays QF Payment Vote  Sources believe that the delay in the PUC vote on paying the QFs 15% of  their undercollected debt is likely a result from both a concern about bankruptcy issues raised by issuing what could be seen as a "preference payment" to the QFs (the PUC does follow these issues out of necessity, given the current environment) and a lack of clarity regarding how to implement the 15% payment.
The delay was unsurprising and characteristic of how the PUC operates.
It is also noted that there are many claims on SoCal's and PG&E's cash flows currently.
Additionally, agreeing to pay 15% of debts to the QFs raises legal issues, in that the utilities would be paying debts to some creditors, but not others.
This could increase the likelihood of an involuntary bankruptcy filing against SoCal by the non-QF creditors.

Dear Greg,  I appreciate you coming down to the gas floor and providing us some information about what is going on.
One of the questions that kept getting asked had to do with who will be retained, and what we will be paid when we are retained.
We were told that star performers will be retained.
At what profit level do we become star performers?
I understand you and your staff have a tremendous number of things that need to be accomplished.
As I talk with my peers, the most important thing on our minds is if we will have a job and what we will be paid.
John was saying that in a few months this issue would be addressed.
My immediate concern is to secure employment while there are still positions available with other companies.
I will accept the first lucrative offer that is made to me.
My peers have expressed the same sentiment.
In a few months, there may not be any jobs left.
We have to may hay while the sun shines.
We all have been bombarded with calls from executive search firms.
We are all racing for a limited number of jobs that promise substantially higher salaries.
What we need on this floor is some assurances.
Maybe it should be in the form of granting bonuses now and offering employment contracts.
We need some exact numbers in the form of dates, salaries, and bonus plans.
Scott Neal brought up this same question several times and John said he understood how critical this situation is.
If there are only trader track personnel left to run this company, will Dynegy still be interested?
Getting a bonus this year that reflects the work I put in is critical.
It is no where near as critical the issue of making sure my children have food on the table.
I do not have two months to wait to find out that the compensation I will be offered ends up being less than what a third party is willing to pay, or the bonus program is a based on a amount to appease me when I may have passed up a percentage deal.
Please sense the urgency that my peers and I are feeling.
Tom Donohoe

**Pipeline Pricing Policy Under FERC Orders 637 and 637-A**

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) established specific rules for how pipeline companies can price their services when existing customers want to renew their contracts at higher rates.

**Key Policy Elements:**

Under Orders 637 and 637-A, when a shipping customer exercises their "Right of First Refusal" (ROFR) to renew service, they may be required to match competing bids that exceed their current maximum rate, but only under these specific conditions:

1. The pipeline has completed an expansion project with new, higher "incremental" rates
2. The pipeline is operating at full capacity 
3. There is a competing bid above the original maximum rate for existing customers

**Rate Adjustment Process:**

To implement these higher matching rates, pipeline companies must establish a formal mechanism that reallocates costs between the original rates and the new expansion rates. This ensures all rates remain within the pipeline's allowable cost-of-service limits.

Pipeline companies can establish this mechanism through either:
- A general section 4 rate case filing
- Pro forma tariff sheets that allow FERC and other parties to review the proposal before implementation

**Historical Example:**

The only referenced case is Viking Gas Transmission Company (1999), where FERC rejected a tariff filing to raise matching rates under ROFR because the company failed to properly readjust existing and expansion rates.

This policy aligns with FERC's 1999 Certificate Policy Statement and ensures fair pricing while protecting both existing customers and promoting pipeline expansion.

The policy spelled out in Order No.
637 (and affirmed on rehearing in Order No.
637-A) for pricing under ROFR at the expiration of a lower-rate service agreement (where rates are "vintaged").
In both Order No 637 and Order No.
637-A the Commission notes that this policy is consistent with the Certificate Policy Statement issued in 1999.
Order No.
637 states as follows:  	[A] shipper exercising its ROFR could be required to match a bid up to a maximum rate higher 	than the historic maximum rate applicable to its capacity in certain limited circumstances:  when a 	pipeline expansion has been completed and an incremental rate exists on the system; the pipeline 	is fully subscribed; and there is a competing bid above the maximum pre-expansion rate applicable 	to existing shippers.
*				*				*  	As the Commission explains in the Certificate Policy Statement, to adjust the maximum rate 	applicable to shippers exercising their ROFR in these circumstances, the pipeline would have to 	establish a mechanism for reallocating costs between the historic and incremental rates so all 	rates remain within the pipeline's cost-of-service.
The mechanism can be established either 	through a general section 4 rate case or through the filing of pro forma tariff sheets which would 	provide the Commission and the parties with an opportunity to review the proposal prior to 	implementation.
Order No.
637 references one instance where a pipeline had filed such a mechanism as follows:  	Cf.
Viking Gas Transmission Company, 89 FERC Para.
61,204 (1999) (rejecting tariff filing to raise 	matching rates under a ROFR where, among other things, the filing did not readjust existing and 	expansion rates.

At the all-employee meeting two weeks ago, I spoke candidly about the major challenges Enron is facing and the urgent steps we are taking to confront them. I also shared with you our vision for Enron to become "The World's Leading Company"—a goal that is not just aspirational, but one that I believe is critical for our survival and our future. 

Your management team and I are fully committed to this goal, and we know that we cannot get there without the passion, resilience, and dedication of every single one of you. Our future depends on how well we come together right now—there is so much at stake for us as individuals, for our families, and for the legacy of Enron itself.

After the all-employee meeting, several of you courageously reached out to share your honest concerns about additional challenges facing Enron. I want to thank you sincerely for your candor. These conversations have underlined just how crucial it is for us to be transparent and to listen to one another as we face these difficult times together.

We have already begun to act on some of the concerns you expressed, but there is more we must know. The next twelve months will be absolutely pivotal for Enron. I am asking—truly asking—all of you to tell me what you believe are the most critical issues facing our company. If you care about this company’s future, if your work here matters to you and your loved ones, this is your moment to speak up.

In other words, I need you to "Lay It on the Line" for me by completing the attached survey. I promise you, your individual answers will remain confidential. The new Management Committee will rely on your input to decide the actions we take—actions that could determine the fate of our company and the security of everyone who relies on it.

We will share the results with you, including the hard truths, and we will be direct about the changes we need to make. Please, take the time to help us. Your voices matter now more than ever. Help us shape Enron’s future and give us the best chance to realize our vision of becoming "The World's Leading Company."

At the all-employee meeting two weeks ago, I talked about the major challenges that I believe Enron is currently facing and what we are doing to address these issues.
I also reviewed with you our vision for Enron to become "The World's Leading Company," and what that means to me.
Your management team and I remain committed to this goal and are confident that by working together, we can achieve this vision.
After the all-employee meeting, a number of you came forward to voice your concerns about what you saw as additional challenges for Enron, and for that, I thank you.
We have already begun working on many of the concerns you expressed.
Now, I would like to hear from more of you about what you see as the most critical issues facing Enron in the next twelve months.
In other words, "Lay It on the Line" for me by completing the attached survey.
I assure you that your individual answers to this survey will remain confidential.
The new Management Committee will use this information to help us identify immediate action steps to address your key concerns.
We will communicate the results to you, both positive and negative, and what we plan to do about them, as soon as we can.
Thank you in advance for taking the time to help us move Enron toward its new vision of becoming "The World's Leading Company."
